// this_file: Tests/DidYouGetTests/RecordingManagerTests.swift

import XCTest
@testable import DidYouGet

final class RecordingManagerTests: XCTestCase {
    
    var recordingManager: RecordingManager!
    var preferencesManager: PreferencesManager!
    
    override func setUp() {
        super.setUp()
        recordingManager = RecordingManager()
        preferencesManager = PreferencesManager()
        recordingManager.setPreferencesManager(preferencesManager)
    }
    
    override func tearDown() {
        recordingManager = nil
        preferencesManager = nil
        super.tearDown()
    }
    
    func testInitialState() {
        XCTAssertFalse(recordingManager.isRecording, "Recording should not be active initially")
        XCTAssertNotNil(recordingManager.preferencesManager, "PreferencesManager should be set")
    }
    
    func testStartRecordingChangesState() {
        // Note: This test may fail if screen recording permission is not granted
        // In a real test environment, you'd mock the permission check
        let initialState = recordingManager.isRecording
        recordingManager.startRecording()
        
        // Give it a moment to start
        let expectation = XCTestExpectation(description: "Recording state change")
        DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.1) {
            expectation.fulfill()
        }
        wait(for: [expectation], timeout: 1.0)
        
        // The state might not change if permissions are not granted
        // This test verifies the method can be called without crashing
        XCTAssertNoThrow(recordingManager.stopRecording())
    }
    
    func testStopRecordingCanBeCalled() {
        XCTAssertNoThrow(recordingManager.stopRecording())
    }
}

<document_content>
//
//  RecordingServiceTests.swift
//  DidYouGetTests
//
//  Tests for RecordingService protocol implementations
//
// this_file: Tests/DidYouGetTests/RecordingServiceTests.swift

import XCTest
@testable import DidYouGet

@MainActor
final class RecordingServiceTests: XCTestCase {
    
    var mockRecordingService: MockRecordingService!
    var mockVideoProcessor: MockVideoProcessor!
    var mockAudioProcessor: MockAudioProcessor!
    var mockPreferences: MockPreferencesProvider!
    
    override func setUp() async throws {
        try await super.setUp()
        mockRecordingService = MockRecordingService()
        mockVideoProcessor = MockVideoProcessor()
        mockAudioProcessor = MockAudioProcessor()
        mockPreferences = MockPreferencesProvider()
    }
    
    override func tearDown() async throws {
        mockRecordingService = nil
        mockVideoProcessor = nil
        mockAudioProcessor = nil
        mockPreferences = nil
        try await super.tearDown()
    }
    
    // MARK: - RecordingService Tests
    
    func testStartRecording() async throws {
        // Given
        let outputURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/test.mp4")
        let config = RecordingConfiguration(
            displayID: CGMainDisplayID(),
            videoSettings: VideoSettings(quality: .high, frameRate: 60),
            outputURL: outputURL
        )
        
        // When
        let session = try await mockRecordingService.startRecording(configuration: config)
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockRecordingService.startRecordingCalled)
        XCTAssertEqual(mockRecordingService.state, .recording)
        XCTAssertNotNil(mockRecordingService.activeRecording)
        XCTAssertEqual(session.configuration, config)
    }
    
    func testStartRecordingFailure() async {
        // Given
        mockRecordingService.shouldFailStart = true
        mockRecordingService.startError = RecordingError.permissionDenied(.screenRecording)
        
        let config = RecordingConfiguration(
            outputURL: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/test.mp4")
        )
        
        // When/Then
        await assertThrowsError {
            _ = try await mockRecordingService.startRecording(configuration: config)
        } errorHandler: { error in
            XCTAssertEqual(error as? RecordingError, RecordingError.permissionDenied(.screenRecording))
        }
    }
    
    func testStopRecording() async throws {
        // Given - Start recording first
        let config = RecordingConfiguration(
            outputURL: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/test.mp4")
        )
        _ = try await mockRecordingService.startRecording(configuration: config)
        
        // When
        let url = try await mockRecordingService.stopRecording()
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockRecordingService.stopRecordingCalled)
        XCTAssertEqual(mockRecordingService.state, .idle)
        XCTAssertNil(mockRecordingService.activeRecording)
        XCTAssertEqual(url, mockRecordingService.mockOutputURL)
    }
    
    func testPauseResume() async {
        // Given
        let config = RecordingConfiguration(
            outputURL: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/test.mp4")
        )
        _ = try? await mockRecordingService.startRecording(configuration: config)
        
        // When - Pause
        await mockRecordingService.pauseRecording()
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockRecordingService.pauseRecordingCalled)
        XCTAssertEqual(mockRecordingService.state, .paused)
        
        // When - Resume
        await mockRecordingService.resumeRecording()
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockRecordingService.resumeRecordingCalled)
        XCTAssertEqual(mockRecordingService.state, .recording)
    }
    
    // MARK: - VideoProcessor Tests
    
    func testVideoProcessorConfiguration() throws {
        // Given
        let settings = VideoSettings(
            codec: .h264,
            resolution: .fullHD,
            frameRate: 60,
            quality: .high
        )
        let outputURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/video.mp4")
        
        // When
        try mockVideoProcessor.configure(settings: settings, outputURL: outputURL)
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockVideoProcessor.configureCalled)
        XCTAssertTrue(mockVideoProcessor.isConfigured)
    }
    
    func testVideoProcessorFrameProcessing() async throws {
        // Given
        try mockVideoProcessor.configure(
            settings: .default,
            outputURL: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/video.mp4")
        )
        
        // Create a test pixel buffer
        var pixelBuffer: CVPixelBuffer?
        let attributes: [String: Any] = [
            kCVPixelBufferCGImageCompatibilityKey as String: true,
            kCVPixelBufferCGBitmapContextCompatibilityKey as String: true
        ]
        CVPixelBufferCreate(
            kCFAllocatorDefault,
            1920, 1080,
            kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA,
            attributes as CFDictionary,
            &pixelBuffer
        )
        
        // When
        if let buffer = pixelBuffer {
            let timestamp = CMTime(value: 0, timescale: 60)
            try await mockVideoProcessor.process(pixelBuffer: buffer, timestamp: timestamp)
        }
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockVideoProcessor.processCalled)
        XCTAssertEqual(mockVideoProcessor.encodedFrameCount, 1)
        XCTAssertEqual(mockVideoProcessor.processedFrames.count, 1)
    }
    
    func testVideoProcessorFinalize() async throws {
        // Given
        try mockVideoProcessor.configure(
            settings: .default,
            outputURL: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/video.mp4")
        )
        
        // When
        try await mockVideoProcessor.finalize()
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockVideoProcessor.finalizeCalled)
        XCTAssertFalse(mockVideoProcessor.isConfigured)
    }
    
    // MARK: - AudioProcessor Tests
    
    func testAudioProcessorConfiguration() throws {
        // Given
        let settings = AudioSettings(
            sampleRate: 48000,
            bitrate: 192000,
            codec: .aac
        )
        
        // When
        try mockAudioProcessor.configureAudio(device: nil, settings: settings)
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockAudioProcessor.configureCalled)
        XCTAssertTrue(mockAudioProcessor.isConfigured)
    }
    
    func testAudioProcessorLifecycle() async throws {
        // Given
        try mockAudioProcessor.configureAudio(device: nil, settings: .default)
        
        // When - Start
        try await mockAudioProcessor.startProcessing()
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockAudioProcessor.startCalled)
        XCTAssertTrue(mockAudioProcessor.isProcessing)
        
        // When - Stop
        try await mockAudioProcessor.stopProcessing()
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockAudioProcessor.stopCalled)
        XCTAssertFalse(mockAudioProcessor.isProcessing)
    }
    
    // MARK: - PreferencesProvider Tests
    
    func testPreferencesSave() async {
        // When
        await mockPreferences.save()
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockPreferences.saveCalled)
    }
    
    func testPreferencesReset() async {
        // Given
        mockPreferences.defaultVideoQuality = .high
        mockPreferences.defaultFrameRate = 60
        mockPreferences.audioEnabled = true
        
        // When
        await mockPreferences.reset()
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockPreferences.resetCalled)
        XCTAssertEqual(mockPreferences.defaultVideoQuality, .medium)
        XCTAssertEqual(mockPreferences.defaultFrameRate, 30)
        XCTAssertFalse(mockPreferences.audioEnabled)
    }
    
    func testPreferencesExport() async throws {
        // Given
        let exportURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/prefs.json")
        
        // When
        try await mockPreferences.export(to: exportURL)
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(mockPreferences.exportCalled)
    }
    
    // MARK: - Integration Tests
    
    func testRecordingConfiguration() {
        // Test configuration creation
        let config = RecordingConfiguration(
            displayID: CGMainDisplayID(),
            captureArea: CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 1920, height: 1080),
            videoSettings: VideoSettings(
                codec: .h265,
                resolution: .fullHD,
                frameRate: 60,
                quality: .high
            ),
            audioSettings: AudioSettings(
                sampleRate: 48000,
                bitrate: 192000,
                codec: .aac
            ),
            outputURL: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/recording.mp4"),
            metadata: RecordingMetadata(
                title: "Test Recording",
                tags: ["test", "demo"]
            )
        )
        
        XCTAssertEqual(config.videoSettings.codec, .h265)
        XCTAssertEqual(config.videoSettings.frameRate, 60)
        XCTAssertEqual(config.audioSettings?.sampleRate, 48000)
        XCTAssertNotNil(config.metadata)
    }
    
    func testRecordingSession() {
        // Test session creation
        let config = RecordingConfiguration(
            outputURL: URL(fileURLWithPath: "/tmp/test.mp4")
        )
        let session = RecordingSession(
            id: UUID(),
            startTime: Date(),
            configuration: config
        )
        
        // Test duration calculation
        XCTAssertGreaterThanOrEqual(session.duration, 0)
        
        // Test file size estimation
        let estimatedSize = session.estimatedFileSize
        XCTAssertGreaterThan(estimatedSize, 0)
    }
}

// MARK: - Test Helpers

func assertThrowsError<T>(
    _ expression: @autoclosure () async throws -> T,
    errorHandler: (Error) -> Void
) async {
    do {
        _ = try await expression()
        XCTFail("Expected error but none was thrown")
    } catch {
        errorHandler(error)
    }
}

<document_content>
// this_file: Tests/DidYouGetTests/VersionManagerTests.swift

import XCTest
@testable import DidYouGet

final class VersionManagerTests: XCTestCase {
    
    func testVersionManagerSingleton() {
        let manager1 = VersionManager.shared
        let manager2 = VersionManager.shared
        XCTAssertTrue(manager1 === manager2, "VersionManager should be a singleton")
    }
    
    func testCurrentVersionIsNotEmpty() {
        let version = VersionManager.shared.currentVersion
        XCTAssertFalse(version.isEmpty, "Current version should not be empty")
    }
    
    func testVersionFormat() {
        let version = VersionManager.shared.currentVersion
        let versionPattern = #"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+.*$"#
        let regex = try! NSRegularExpression(pattern: versionPattern)
        let range = NSRange(location: 0, length: version.utf16.count)
        let match = regex.firstMatch(in: version, options: [], range: range)
        XCTAssertNotNil(match, "Version should follow semantic versioning format")
    }
    
    func testBuildNumberIsNumeric() {
        let buildNumber = VersionManager.shared.buildNumber
        XCTAssertTrue(Int(buildNumber) != nil, "Build number should be numeric")
    }
    
    func testCommitHashIsNotEmpty() {
        let commitHash = VersionManager.shared.commitHash
        XCTAssertFalse(commitHash.isEmpty, "Commit hash should not be empty")
    }
    
    func testFullVersionString() {
        let fullVersion = VersionManager.shared.fullVersionString
        XCTAssertFalse(fullVersion.isEmpty, "Full version string should not be empty")
        XCTAssertTrue(fullVersion.contains("build"), "Full version should contain build info")
    }
}

# Work Progress

## Current Session: Code Improvements and Documentation

### Completed Tasks

1. **Documentation Infrastructure** ✅
   - Set up complete MkDocs documentation structure in `src_docs/`
   - Created comprehensive user guides:
     - Installation guide
     - Quick start guide
     - Configuration guide
     - Troubleshooting guide
   - Created feature documentation:
     - Screen recording
     - Audio recording
     - Input tracking
     - Output formats
   - Created development documentation:
     - Architecture overview
     - Building guide
     - Testing guide
     - Contributing guide
   - Created API reference documentation:
     - Core API
     - Recording services
     - UI components
   - Added build script (`build-docs.sh`) for documentation generation

2. **Protocol-Based Architecture** ✅
   - Created `RecordingProtocols.swift` with comprehensive protocol definitions:
     - `RecordingService` - Main recording interface
     - `VideoProcessing` - Video processing interface
     - `AudioProcessing` - Audio processing interface
     - `CaptureSessionProtocol` - Capture session interface
     - `PreferencesProviding` - Preferences interface
   - Implemented protocol conformances:
     - `RecordingManager+Protocol.swift`
     - `VideoProcessor+Protocol.swift`
     - `AudioProcessor+Protocol.swift`
     - `PreferencesManager+Protocol.swift`
   - Created mock implementations for testing:
     - `MockRecordingService`
     - `MockVideoProcessor`
     - `MockAudioProcessor`
     - `MockPreferencesProvider`
   - Created protocol-based tests in `RecordingServiceTests.swift`

3. **Async/Await Migration** ✅
   - Created `SCStreamFrameOutput+Async.swift` with AsyncStream-based frame delivery
   - Created `AsyncFrameProcessor` for concurrent frame processing
   - Created `CaptureSessionManager+Async.swift` with async stream processing
   - Migrated from callback-based to async/await patterns

4. **Error Types and Logging Infrastructure** ✅
   - Created comprehensive `Logger.swift` with:
     - Multiple log levels (verbose, debug, info, warning, error, critical)
     - Category-based logging
     - OS Log integration
     - File logging support
     - Performance measurement utilities
   - Created detailed error types in `Errors.swift`:
     - `VideoError` - Video-specific errors
     - `AudioError` - Audio-specific errors
     - `CaptureError` - Capture-specific errors
     - `FileError` - File operation errors
     - `StateError` - State management errors
     - `ConfigurationError` - Configuration errors
   - Added error recovery suggestions for all error types

5. **Singleton Pattern Implementation** ✅
   - Created `RecordingManager+Singleton.swift`
   - Implemented thread-safe singleton for `RecordingManager`
   - Created `ManagerRegistry` for centralized manager access
   - Added singleton support for `PreferencesManager` and `VersionManager`

### Next Tasks

1. **Fix AVAssetWriter Issues**
   - Remove non-standard video compression keys
   - Implement fallback settings for unsupported configurations
   - Add comprehensive error handling around writer creation

2. **Improve State Management**
   - Fix recording state persistence issues
   - Implement proper state restoration
   - Add state validation before operations

3. **Create Unit Tests**
   - Expand test coverage to 80%+
   - Add integration tests for recording pipeline
   - Create UI tests for critical flows

4. **Performance Optimization**
   - Profile CPU and memory usage
   - Optimize buffer management
   - Implement frame dropping strategy

### Technical Decisions Made

1. **Protocol-Oriented Design**: Adopted protocol-based architecture for better testability and flexibility
2. **Async/Await**: Migrated from callbacks to modern Swift concurrency
3. **Structured Logging**: Implemented comprehensive logging with categories and levels
4. **Error Handling**: Created detailed error types with recovery suggestions
5. **Documentation**: Used MkDocs with Material theme for comprehensive documentation

### Issues Encountered

1. **Compatibility**: Maintained backward compatibility while introducing new patterns
2. **Testing**: Need to expand test coverage significantly
3. **Performance**: Frame processing needs optimization for high frame rates

### Code Quality Improvements

- Added proper error types instead of NSError
- Implemented structured logging instead of print statements
- Created protocol abstractions for better testability
- Migrated to async/await for cleaner async code
- Added comprehensive documentation

### Files Modified/Created

#### Created Files:
- `/src_docs/` - Complete documentation structure
- `RecordingProtocols.swift` - Protocol definitions
- `*+Protocol.swift` files - Protocol conformances
- `MockRecordingService.swift` - Test mocks

- `Logger.swift` - Logging infrastructure
- `Errors.swift` - Error types
- `RecordingManager+Singleton.swift` - Singleton implementation

#### Modified Files:

- Various existing files updated with new imports

### Outstanding Questions

1. Should we make manager initializers private to enforce singleton pattern?
2. Should we migrate all print statements to use the new logger?
3. Should we create a dependency injection container for better testability?

### Notes

- Documentation is ready to be built with `./build-docs.sh`
- All new code follows Swift best practices and modern patterns
- Backward compatibility maintained where possible
- Focus on testability and maintainability

<source>build-docs.sh</source>
<document_content>
#!/bin/bash
# this_file: build-docs.sh

set -e

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
SRC_DOCS_DIR="src_docs"
BUILD_DIR="docs"
SITE_DIR="site"

echo -e "${GREEN}Building Did You Get It Documentation${NC}"
echo "========================================"

# Check if mkdocs is installed
if ! command -v mkdocs &> /dev/null; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}MkDocs not found. Installing...${NC}"
    pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material mkdocstrings[python]
fi

# Clean previous builds
if [ -d "$BUILD_DIR" ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Cleaning previous documentation build...${NC}"
    rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR"
fi

if [ -d "$SITE_DIR" ]; then
    rm -rf "$SITE_DIR"
fi

# Create build directory
mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"

# Copy documentation files
echo -e "${GREEN}Copying documentation files...${NC}"
cp -r "$SRC_DOCS_DIR"/* "$BUILD_DIR/"

# Build the documentation
echo -e "${GREEN}Building documentation site...${NC}"
cd "$BUILD_DIR"
mkdocs build

# Move site to root
cd ..
if [ -d "$BUILD_DIR/site" ]; then
    mv "$BUILD_DIR/site" .
    echo -e "${GREEN}Documentation built successfully!${NC}"
    echo -e "View at: ${YELLOW}file://$(pwd)/site/index.html${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${RED}Documentation build failed!${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

# Optional: Serve locally
if [ "$1" = "--serve" ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}Starting documentation server...${NC}"
    cd "$BUILD_DIR"
    mkdocs serve
fi
</document_content>
</document>

<document_content>
#!/bin/bash

# build.sh - Build script with versioning support
# Usage: ./build.sh [debug|release] [--test] [--clean]

set -e

# Configuration
APP_NAME="DidYouGet"
BUNDLE_ID="it.didyouget.mac"
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
BUILD_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/.build"
RELEASE_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/release"

# Default options
BUILD_TYPE="debug"
RUN_TESTS=false
CLEAN_BUILD=false

# Parse arguments
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in
        debug|release)
            BUILD_TYPE="$1"
            shift
            ;;
        --test)
            RUN_TESTS=true
            shift
            ;;
        --clean)
            CLEAN_BUILD=true
            shift
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown option: $1"
            echo "Usage: $0 [debug|release] [--test] [--clean]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
done

cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

# Check if Swift is available
if ! command -v swift &> /dev/null; then
    echo "❌ Swift is not installed or not in PATH"
    echo "Please install Swift from https://swift.org/download/"
    exit 1
fi

# Clean if requested
if [ "$CLEAN_BUILD" = true ]; then
    echo "🧹 Cleaning build artifacts..."
    rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR"
    rm -rf "$RELEASE_DIR"
    swift package clean
fi

# Get version information
VERSION=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || echo "1.0.0")
VERSION_CLEAN=$(echo "$VERSION" | sed 's/^v//')
BUILD_NUMBER=$(git rev-list --count HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
COMMIT_HASH=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
IS_RELEASE=$(git describe --tags --exact-match HEAD 2>/dev/null && echo "true" || echo "false")

if [ "$IS_RELEASE" = "true" ]; then
    FULL_VERSION="$VERSION_CLEAN (build $BUILD_NUMBER)"
else
    FULL_VERSION="$VERSION_CLEAN-dev (build $BUILD_NUMBER, commit $COMMIT_HASH)"
fi

echo "📦 Building $APP_NAME"
echo "   Version: $FULL_VERSION"
echo "   Build Type: $BUILD_TYPE"
echo "   Run Tests: $RUN_TESTS"

# Run tests if requested
if [ "$RUN_TESTS" = true ]; then
    echo "🧪 Running tests..."
    swift test --parallel
    echo "✅ Tests passed!"
fi

# Build the application
echo "🔨 Building application..."
if [ "$BUILD_TYPE" = "release" ]; then
    swift build -c release
    APP_PATH="$(swift build -c release --show-bin-path)/$APP_NAME"
else
    swift build
    APP_PATH="$(swift build --show-bin-path)/$APP_NAME"
fi

# Verify build
if [ ! -f "$APP_PATH" ]; then
    echo "❌ Build failed. Could not find executable at $APP_PATH"
    exit 1
fi

echo "✅ Build successful!"
echo "   Executable: $APP_PATH"
echo "   Version: $FULL_VERSION"

# Create release package if building for release
if [ "$BUILD_TYPE" = "release" ]; then
    echo "📦 Creating release package..."
    mkdir -p "$RELEASE_DIR"
    
    # Copy executable
    cp "$APP_PATH" "$RELEASE_DIR/"
    
    # Create version info file
    cat > "$RELEASE_DIR/version.txt" << EOF
$APP_NAME $FULL_VERSION
Built: $(date)
Platform: macOS
EOF
    
    # Create archive
    cd "$RELEASE_DIR"
    tar -czf "$APP_NAME-$VERSION_CLEAN-macos.tar.gz" "$APP_NAME" version.txt
    
    echo "✅ Release package created: $RELEASE_DIR/$APP_NAME-$VERSION_CLEAN-macos.tar.gz"
fi

echo "🎉 Build complete!"
</document_content>
</document>

#!/bin/bash

# install.sh - Install DidYouGet to Applications folder
# Usage: ./install.sh [--force]

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
APP_NAME="DidYouGet"
INSTALL_DIR="/Applications"
FORCE_INSTALL=false

# Parse arguments
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in
        --force)
            FORCE_INSTALL=true
            shift
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown option: $1"
            echo "Usage: $0 [--force]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
done

cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

echo "📦 Installing $APP_NAME"

# Check if already installed
if [ -d "$INSTALL_DIR/$APP_NAME.app" ] && [ "$FORCE_INSTALL" = false ]; then
    echo "⚠️  $APP_NAME is already installed in $INSTALL_DIR"
    read -p "Overwrite existing installation? (y/N) " -n 1 -r
    echo
    if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
        echo "❌ Installation cancelled"
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# Build release version
echo "🔨 Building release version..."
./build.sh release --test

# Get version info
VERSION=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || echo "1.0.0")
VERSION_CLEAN=$(echo "$VERSION" | sed 's/^v//')

# Create app bundle structure
APP_BUNDLE="$SCRIPT_DIR/build/$APP_NAME.app"
CONTENTS_DIR="$APP_BUNDLE/Contents"
MACOS_DIR="$CONTENTS_DIR/MacOS"
RESOURCES_DIR="$CONTENTS_DIR/Resources"

echo "📁 Creating app bundle..."
mkdir -p "$MACOS_DIR"
mkdir -p "$RESOURCES_DIR"

# Copy executable
cp ".build/release/$APP_NAME" "$MACOS_DIR/"

# Create Info.plist
cat > "$CONTENTS_DIR/Info.plist" << EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>CFBundleExecutable</key>
    <string>$APP_NAME</string>
    <key>CFBundleIdentifier</key>
    <string>it.didyouget.mac</string>
    <key>CFBundleName</key>
    <string>$APP_NAME</string>
    <key>CFBundleVersion</key>
    <string>$VERSION_CLEAN</string>
    <key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key>
    <string>$VERSION_CLEAN</string>
    <key>CFBundlePackageType</key>
    <string>APPL</string>
    <key>CFBundleSignature</key>
    <string>????</string>
    <key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key>
    <string>13.0</string>
    <key>LSUIElement</key>
    <true/>
    <key>NSHighResolutionCapable</key>
    <true/>
    <key>NSSupportsAutomaticGraphicsSwitching</key>
    <true/>
</dict>
</plist>
EOF

# Copy to Applications (requires admin privileges)
echo "📥 Installing to $INSTALL_DIR..."
if [ -w "$INSTALL_DIR" ]; then
    # Can write directly
    rm -rf "$INSTALL_DIR/$APP_NAME.app"
    cp -R "$APP_BUNDLE" "$INSTALL_DIR/"
else
    # Need sudo
    sudo rm -rf "$INSTALL_DIR/$APP_NAME.app"
    sudo cp -R "$APP_BUNDLE" "$INSTALL_DIR/"
fi

# Verify installation
if [ -d "$INSTALL_DIR/$APP_NAME.app" ]; then
    echo "✅ $APP_NAME installed successfully!"
    echo "   Location: $INSTALL_DIR/$APP_NAME.app"
    echo "   Version: $VERSION_CLEAN"
    echo ""
    echo "🚀 You can now launch $APP_NAME from:"
    echo "   - Applications folder"
    echo "   - Spotlight search"
    echo "   - Command line: open -a $APP_NAME"
else
    echo "❌ Installation failed"
    exit 1
fi

echo "🎉 Installation complete!"
</document_content>
</document>

#!/bin/bash

# run.sh - Build and run Did You Get It app
# Usage: ./run.sh [debug|release]

set -e

# Default to debug build
BUILD_TYPE=${1:-debug}
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

# Check if the directory structure exists
if [ ! -d "DidYouGet/DidYouGet" ]; then
    echo "Error: DidYouGet directory structure not found."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Building Did You Get It app in $BUILD_TYPE mode..."

if [ "$BUILD_TYPE" = "release" ]; then
    # Release build
    swift build -c release
    APP_PATH="$(swift build -c release --show-bin-path)/DidYouGet"
else
    # Debug build
    swift build
    APP_PATH="$(swift build --show-bin-path)/DidYouGet"
fi

# Check if build succeeded
if [ ! -f "$APP_PATH" ]; then
    echo "Error: Build failed. Could not find executable at $APP_PATH"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Build successful!"
echo "Running application from: $APP_PATH"

# Run the app
"$APP_PATH"

# 7. Advanced Usage

## Automation and Scripting

### AppleScript Integration

#### Recording Control via AppleScript
Did You Get It provides comprehensive AppleScript support for workflow automation:

```applescript
-- Start recording with custom configuration
tell application "Did You Get It"
    start recording with properties {
        recording area: {x:100, y:100, width:1200, height:800},
        frame rate: 60,
        include system audio: true,
        include microphone: false,
        output location: "~/Desktop/Recordings/"
    }
end tell

-- Stop recording and get file paths
tell application "Did You Get It"
    set recording_files to stop recording
    return recording_files
end tell

-- Get current recording status
tell application "Did You Get It"
    set current_status to recording status
    set recording_time to recording duration
    
    if current_status is "recording" then
        display notification "Recording in progress: " & recording_time
    end if
end tell
```

#### Advanced AppleScript Examples
```applescript
-- Automated testing scenario
on run
    tell application "Did You Get It"
        -- Configure for high-precision input tracking
        set configuration to {
            recording area: entire screen,
            frame rate: 60,
            mouse precision: "high",
            keyboard tracking: true,
            include system audio: true
        }
        
        start recording with properties configuration
        
        -- Wait for external test completion signal
        repeat while recording status is "recording"
            delay 1
            if (do shell script "test -f /tmp/stop_recording && echo 'true' || echo 'false'") is "true" then
                exit repeat
            end if
        end repeat
        
        set output_files to stop recording
        
        -- Process the recorded data
        repeat with file_path in output_files
            if file_path contains "mouse_events.json" then
                do shell script "python3 ~/Scripts/analyze_mouse_data.py " & quoted form of file_path
            end if
        end repeat
    end tell
end run
```

### Shortcuts App Integration

#### Shortcuts Actions
```swift
// Custom shortcuts intent for recording control
class StartRecordingIntent: INIntent {
    @NSManaged public var recordingArea: RecordingAreaType
    @NSManaged public var frameRate: NSNumber?
    @NSManaged public var includeAudio: NSNumber?
    @NSManaged public var outputLocation: String?
}

@available(iOS 16.0, macOS 13.0, *)
struct StartRecordingShortcut: AppIntent {
    static var title: LocalizedStringResource = "Start Recording"
    static var description = IntentDescription("Starts a new recording session with specified parameters")
    
    @Parameter(title: "Recording Area", default: .fullScreen)
    var recordingArea: RecordingAreaType
    
    @Parameter(title: "Frame Rate", default: 60)
    var frameRate: Int
    
    @Parameter(title: "Include System Audio", default: true)
    var includeAudio: Bool
    
    func perform() async throws -> some IntentResult {
        let configuration = RecordingConfiguration(
            area: recordingArea.area,
            frameRate: frameRate,
            systemAudio: includeAudio
        )
        
        try await RecordingManager.shared.startRecording(with: configuration)
        
        return .result(dialog: "Recording started successfully")
    }
}
```

```swift
// Xcode build phase script for automated testing recordings
#!/bin/bash

# Start recording before running tests
/Applications/Did\ You\ Get\ It.app/Contents/MacOS/CLI/dygi start \
    --area=screen \
    --fps=30 \
```

#### Visual Studio Code Extension
```typescript
// VSCode extension integration example
import * as vscode from 'vscode';
import { exec } from 'child_process';

export function activate(context: vscode.ExtensionContext) {
    let startRecording = vscode.commands.registerCommand('didyougetit.startRecording', () => {
        const config = vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('didyougetit');
        const recordingArea = config.get('recordingArea', 'screen');
        const frameRate = config.get('frameRate', 60);
        
        exec(`dygi start --area=${recordingArea} --fps=${frameRate}`, (error, stdout, stderr) => {
            if (error) {
                vscode.window.showErrorMessage(`Recording failed: ${error.message}`);
                return;
            }
            vscode.window.showInformationMessage('Recording started');
        });
    });
    
    context.subscriptions.push(startRecording);
}
```

### CI/CD Pipeline Integration

#### GitHub Actions Workflow
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ui-testing-with-recording.yml
name: UI Testing with Screen Recording

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'tests/**'

jobs:
  ui-tests-with-recording:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Setup Did You Get It
      run: |
        # Install or configure Did You Get It for CI
        curl -L https://github.com/twardoch/didyougetit-mac/releases/latest/download/DidYouGetIt-CLI.zip -o cli.zip
        unzip cli.zip
        chmod +x dygi
        
    - name: Run UI Tests with Recording
      run: |
        # Start recording
        ./dygi start --area=screen --fps=30 --name="ui_test_${{ github.run_number }}" &
        RECORDING_PID=$!
        
        # Run UI tests
        npm run test:ui
        
        # Stop recording
        kill $RECORDING_PID
        ./dygi stop
        
    - name: Upload Recording Artifacts
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      if: failure()
      with:
        name: ui-test-recordings
        path: ~/Recordings/ui_test_*
        retention-days: 7
```

```groovy
pipeline {
    agent { label 'macos' }

            steps {
                script {
                    sh '''
                        # Configure recording for test environment
                        dygi config set --profile=ci \
                            --frame-rate=24 \
                            --resolution=1080p \
                            --audio=false \
                            --output="/tmp/recordings"
                    '''
                }
            }

        stage('Run Tests with Recording') {
            steps {
                script {

                        sh 'dygi start --profile=ci --name="build_${BUILD_NUMBER}"'
                        sh 'make test-ui'
                    } finally {
                        sh 'dygi stop'
                        
                        // Archive recordings for failed tests
                        if (currentBuild.result == 'FAILURE') {
                            archiveArtifacts artifacts: '/tmp/recordings/**/*', fingerprint: true
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Data Analysis and Processing

### JSON Data Processing

#### Python Analysis Scripts
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Analyze mouse and keyboard interaction data from Did You Get It recordings.
"""

import json
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

class RecordingAnalyzer:
    def __init__(self, session_path):
        self.session_path = session_path
        self.mouse_data = self.load_mouse_data()
        self.keyboard_data = self.load_keyboard_data()
        
    def load_mouse_data(self):
        """Load and parse mouse events JSON."""
        with open(f"{self.session_path}/input_data/mouse_events.json", 'r') as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        
        df = pd.DataFrame(data['mouse_events'])
        df['timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(df['timestamp'], unit='s')
        return df
    
    def analyze_click_patterns(self):
        """Analyze clicking behavior patterns."""
        clicks = self.mouse_data[self.mouse_data['type'] == 'click']
        
        # Calculate click frequency over time
        click_frequency = clicks.groupby(clicks['timestamp'].dt.floor('1min')).size()
        
        # Identify click hotspots
        hotspots = clicks.groupby(['x', 'y']).size().sort_values(ascending=False).head(10)
        
        return {
            'total_clicks': len(clicks),
            'click_frequency': click_frequency.to_dict(),
            'hotspots': hotspots.to_dict()
        }
    
    def generate_heatmap(self, output_path="mouse_heatmap.png"):
        """Generate mouse movement heatmap."""
        moves = self.mouse_data[self.mouse_data['type'] == 'move']
        
        plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
        plt.hexbin(moves['x'], moves['y'], gridsize=50, cmap='hot')
        plt.colorbar(label='Movement Frequency')
        plt.title('Mouse Movement Heatmap')
        plt.xlabel('X Coordinate')
        plt.ylabel('Y Coordinate')
        plt.savefig(output_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
        
    def export_for_ux_analysis(self, output_path="ux_analysis.csv"):
        """Export data in format suitable for UX analysis tools."""
        # Combine mouse and keyboard events with timing
        events = []
        
        for _, row in self.mouse_data.iterrows():
            events.append({
                'timestamp': row['timestamp'],
                'event_type': 'mouse',
                'action': row['type'],
                'x': row.get('x'),
                'y': row.get('y'),
                'details': json.dumps(row.to_dict())
            })
        
        for _, row in self.keyboard_data.iterrows():
            events.append({
                'timestamp': row['timestamp'],
                'event_type': 'keyboard',
                'action': row['type'],
                'x': None,
                'y': None,
                'details': json.dumps(row.to_dict())
            })
        
        df = pd.DataFrame(events).sort_values('timestamp')
        df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

# Usage example
analyzer = RecordingAnalyzer("~/Recordings/user_test_session")
patterns = analyzer.analyze_click_patterns()
analyzer.generate_heatmap()
analyzer.export_for_ux_analysis()
```

#### R Analysis Example
```r
# R script for statistical analysis of interaction data
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Load recording data
load_recording_data <- function(session_path) {
  mouse_file <- file.path(session_path, "input_data", "mouse_events.json")
  keyboard_file <- file.path(session_path, "input_data", "keyboard_events.json")
  
  mouse_data <- fromJSON(mouse_file)$mouse_events
  keyboard_data <- fromJSON(keyboard_file)$keyboard_events
  
  list(mouse = mouse_data, keyboard = keyboard_data)
}

# Analyze user efficiency metrics
analyze_efficiency <- function(data) {
  mouse_df <- data$mouse %>%
    mutate(timestamp = as_datetime(timestamp)) %>%
    arrange(timestamp)
  
  # Calculate movement efficiency (distance vs. time)
  mouse_df <- mouse_df %>%
    mutate(
      distance = sqrt((x - lag(x))^2 + (y - lag(y))^2),
      time_diff = as.numeric(timestamp - lag(timestamp))
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(distance), time_diff > 0)
  
  # Movement efficiency metrics
  total_distance <- sum(mouse_df$distance, na.rm = TRUE)
  total_time <- max(mouse_df$timestamp) - min(mouse_df$timestamp)
  avg_speed <- total_distance / as.numeric(total_time)
  
  list(
    total_distance = total_distance,
    total_time = total_time,
    average_speed = avg_speed,
    movement_efficiency = total_distance / as.numeric(total_time)
  )
}
```

### Machine Learning Integration

#### Gesture Recognition Model
```python
"""
Train a gesture recognition model from Did You Get It input data.
"""

import tensorflow as tf
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
import numpy as np

class GestureRecognizer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.model = self.build_model()
        self.sequence_length = 50  # 50 events per sequence
        
    def build_model(self):
        """Build LSTM model for gesture recognition."""
        model = tf.keras.Sequential([
            tf.keras.layers.LSTM(128, return_sequences=True, input_shape=(50, 4)),
            tf.keras.layers.Dropout(0.2),
            tf.keras.layers.LSTM(64, return_sequences=False),
            tf.keras.layers.Dropout(0.2),
            tf.keras.layers.Dense(32, activation='relu'),
            tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')  # 10 gesture classes
        ])
        
        model.compile(
            optimizer='adam',
            loss='categorical_crossentropy',
            metrics=['accuracy']
        )
        
        return model
    
    def preprocess_recording(self, session_path):
        """Convert recording data to model input format."""
        with open(f"{session_path}/input_data/mouse_events.json") as f:
            mouse_data = json.load(f)['mouse_events']
        
        # Extract features: x, y, timestamp, event_type_encoded
        sequences = []
        for i in range(len(mouse_data) - self.sequence_length + 1):
            sequence = []
            for j in range(i, i + self.sequence_length):
                event = mouse_data[j]
                features = [
                    event['x'] / 1920.0,  # Normalize coordinates
                    event['y'] / 1080.0,
                    event['timestamp'],
                    1.0 if event['type'] == 'click' else 0.0
                ]
                sequence.append(features)
            sequences.append(sequence)
        
        return np.array(sequences)
    
    def train(self, training_sessions, labels):
        """Train the model on multiple recording sessions."""
        X = []
        y = []
        
        for session_path, label in zip(training_sessions, labels):
            sequences = self.preprocess_recording(session_path)
            X.extend(sequences)
            y.extend([label] * len(sequences))
        
        X = np.array(X)
        y = tf.keras.utils.to_categorical(y, 10)
        
        X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2)
        
        self.model.fit(
            X_train, y_train,
            validation_data=(X_val, y_val),
            epochs=50,
            batch_size=32
        )
```

## Workflow Automation Examples

### Testing Workflow Automation
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# automated_testing.sh - Complete testing workflow with recording

set -e

PROJECT_DIR="$1"
TEST_SUITE="$2"
RECORDING_NAME="test_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"

echo "Starting automated testing workflow..."

# Setup recording environment
dygi config set --profile=testing \
    --frame-rate=30 \
    --resolution=1080p \
    --audio=system \
    --mouse-precision=high \
    --keyboard-tracking=true

# Start recording
echo "Starting recording: $RECORDING_NAME"
dygi start --profile=testing --name="$RECORDING_NAME"

# Run the test suite
echo "Running test suite: $TEST_SUITE"
cd "$PROJECT_DIR"

case "$TEST_SUITE" in
    "ui")
        npm run test:ui || TEST_FAILED=true
        ;;
    "integration")
        python -m pytest tests/integration/ || TEST_FAILED=true
        ;;
    "manual")
        echo "Perform manual testing now. Press Enter when complete."
        read -r
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Unknown test suite: $TEST_SUITE"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

# Stop recording
echo "Stopping recording..."
RECORDING_FILES=$(dygi stop --json | jq -r '.files[]')

# Process results
if [ "$TEST_FAILED" = true ]; then
    echo "Tests failed. Processing recording for analysis..."
    
    # Extract failure screenshots
    dygi extract-frames \
        --video="$RECORDING_FILES" \
        --interval=1 \
        --output="screenshots/"
    
    # Generate interaction report
    python3 scripts/analyze_test_failure.py \
        --recording="$RECORDING_FILES" \
        --test-results="test_results.xml" \
        --output="failure_analysis.html"
    
    echo "Failure analysis complete. Check failure_analysis.html"
else
    echo "All tests passed!"
    
    # Archive successful recording for regression testing
    mkdir -p "test_baselines/"
    cp -r "$RECORDING_FILES" "test_baselines/"
fi
```

### Content Creation Pipeline
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Automated content creation pipeline using Did You Get It recordings.
"""

import subprocess
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

class ContentCreationPipeline:
    def __init__(self, project_config):
        self.config = project_config
        self.session_name = f"content_{project_config['name']}"
        
    def record_demonstration(self):
        """Start recording with optimized settings for content creation."""
        cmd = [
            "dygi", "start",
            "--name", self.session_name,
            "--frame-rate", "60",
            "--resolution", "native",
            "--audio", "system,microphone",
            "--cursor", "highlight",
            "--area", self.config.get("recording_area", "screen")
        ]
        
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
        print(f"Recording started: {self.session_name}")
        print("Perform your demonstration now...")
        
        # Wait for user to complete demonstration
        input("Press Enter when demonstration is complete...")
        
        # Stop recording and get file paths
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["dygi", "stop", "--json"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True
        )
        
        return json.loads(result.stdout)
    
    def post_process_recording(self, recording_data):
        """Apply post-processing to enhance the recording."""
        video_file = recording_data["files"]["video"]
        
        # Generate thumbnail timeline
        subprocess.run([
            "ffmpeg", "-i", video_file,
            "-vf", "fps=1/10,scale=320:180",
            f"{self.session_name}_timeline_%03d.jpg"
        ], check=True)
        
        # Create chapters from input data
        self.create_chapters(recording_data["files"]["mouse_events"])
        
        # Generate captions from audio
        if "audio" in recording_data["files"]:
            self.generate_captions(recording_data["files"]["audio"])
    
    def create_chapters(self, mouse_events_file):
        """Create video chapters based on interaction patterns."""
        with open(mouse_events_file) as f:
            events = json.load(f)
        
        # Identify chapter breaks (periods of inactivity)
        chapters = []
        last_event_time = 0
        chapter_start = 0
        
        for event in events["mouse_events"]:
            if event["timestamp"] - last_event_time > 3:  # 3 seconds gap
                if last_event_time > 0:
                    chapters.append({
                        "start": chapter_start,
                        "end": last_event_time,
                        "title": f"Chapter {len(chapters) + 1}"
                    })
                chapter_start = event["timestamp"]
            last_event_time = event["timestamp"]
        
        # Save chapters file
        with open(f"{self.session_name}_chapters.json", "w") as f:
            json.dump(chapters, f, indent=2)

# Usage
config = {
    "name": "app_tutorial",
    "recording_area": "application:Xcode"
}

pipeline = ContentCreationPipeline(config)
recording_data = pipeline.record_demonstration()
pipeline.post_process_recording(recording_data)
```

Ready to troubleshoot issues? Continue to [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) for comprehensive problem-solving guidance.

# 6. Configuration & Settings

## Settings Architecture

### Preferences Storage System

#### UserDefaults Integration
Did You Get It uses a sophisticated preferences system built on UserDefaults with type safety and validation:

```swift
@propertyWrapper
struct UserDefault<T> {
    let key: String
    let defaultValue: T
    
    var wrappedValue: T {
        get {
            UserDefaults.standard.object(forKey: key) as? T ?? defaultValue
        }
        set {
            UserDefaults.standard.set(newValue, forKey: key)
        }
    }
}

class PreferencesManager: ObservableObject {
    // Video settings
    @UserDefault(key: "recording.frameRate", defaultValue: 60)
    @Published var frameRate: Int
    
    @UserDefault(key: "recording.resolution", defaultValue: "native")
    @Published var resolution: String
    
    @UserDefault(key: "recording.showCursor", defaultValue: true)
    @Published var showCursor: Bool
    
    // Audio settings
    @UserDefault(key: "audio.systemEnabled", defaultValue: true)
    @Published var systemAudioEnabled: Bool
    
    @UserDefault(key: "audio.microphoneEnabled", defaultValue: false)
    @Published var microphoneEnabled: Bool
}
```

#### Configuration Validation
```swift
protocol ConfigurationValidator {
    func validate(_ configuration: RecordingConfiguration) throws
}

struct RecordingConfigurationValidator: ConfigurationValidator {
    func validate(_ configuration: RecordingConfiguration) throws {
        // Validate video settings
        guard configuration.frameRate > 0 && configuration.frameRate <= 120 else {
            throw ValidationError.invalidFrameRate(configuration.frameRate)
        }
        
        // Validate recording area
        guard configuration.recordingArea.width > 0 && configuration.recordingArea.height > 0 else {
            throw ValidationError.invalidRecordingArea
        }
        
        // Validate output location
        guard FileManager.default.isWritableFile(atPath: configuration.outputLocation.path) else {
            throw ValidationError.inaccessibleOutputLocation(configuration.outputLocation)
        }
    }
}
```

```swift
enum FrameRate: Int, CaseIterable, Identifiable {
    case fps24 = 24
    case fps30 = 30
    case fps60 = 60
    case fps120 = 120
    
    var id: Int { rawValue }
    
    var displayName: String {
        switch self {
        case .fps24: return "24 FPS (Cinematic)"
        case .fps30: return "30 FPS (Standard)"
        case .fps60: return "60 FPS (Smooth)"
        case .fps120: return "120 FPS (Ultra Smooth)"
        }
    }
    
    var recommendedFor: String {
        switch self {
        case .fps24: return "Film-like content, long recordings"
        case .fps30: return "General tutorials, presentations"
        case .fps60: return "Smooth UI demonstrations"
        case .fps120: return "High-motion content, gaming"
        }
    }
}
```

#### Dynamic Frame Rate Adjustment
```swift
class AdaptiveFrameRateManager {
    private var targetFrameRate: Int
    private var currentFrameRate: Int = 0
    private let performanceMonitor: PerformanceMonitor
    
    func adjustFrameRateIfNeeded() {
        let systemLoad = performanceMonitor.cpuUsage
        let memoryPressure = performanceMonitor.memoryPressure
        
        if systemLoad > 0.8 || memoryPressure > 0.9 {
            // Reduce frame rate to maintain system performance
            let adjustedRate = max(24, targetFrameRate / 2)
            updateFrameRate(to: adjustedRate)
        }
    }
}
```

### Resolution Settings

#### Resolution Presets
```swift
enum Resolution: String, CaseIterable {
    case native = "native"
    case retina2x = "retina2x"
    case fullHD = "1080p"
    case quadHD = "1440p"
    case ultraHD = "4k"
    case custom = "custom"
    
    var dimensions: (width: Int, height: Int) {
        switch self {
        case .native:
            return getCurrentDisplayResolution()
        case .retina2x:
            let native = getCurrentDisplayResolution()
            return (native.width / 2, native.height / 2)
        case .fullHD:
            return (1920, 1080)
        case .quadHD:
            return (2560, 1440)
        case .ultraHD:
            return (3840, 2160)
        case .custom:
            return getCustomResolution()
        }
    }
}
```

#### Custom Resolution Configuration
```swift
struct CustomResolution {
    var width: Int
    var height: Int
    
    var aspectRatio: Double {
        return Double(width) / Double(height)
    }
    
    var isValid: Bool {
        return width >= 320 && height >= 240 && width <= 7680 && height <= 4320
    }
    
    static let commonAspectRatios: [(ratio: Double, name: String)] = [
        (16.0/9.0, "16:9 Widescreen"),
        (4.0/3.0, "4:3 Standard"),
        (21.0/9.0, "21:9 Ultrawide"),
        (1.0, "1:1 Square")
    ]
}
```

```swift
        case .medium: return 0.6
        case .low: return 0.4
        case .custom: return 1.0 // User-defined
        }
```

## Output and File Settings

### File Naming and Organization

#### Naming Templates
```swift
struct FileNamingSettings {
    var template: String = "recording_{date}_{time}"
    var dateFormat: String = "yyyy-MM-dd"
    var timeFormat: String = "HH-mm-ss"
    var includeSequenceNumber: Bool = false
    var customPrefix: String = ""
    var customSuffix: String = ""
    
    // Available template variables
    static let availableVariables = [
        "{date}": "Current date",
        "{time}": "Current time",
        "{duration}": "Recording duration",
        "{resolution}": "Recording resolution",
        "{fps}": "Frame rate",
        "{display}": "Display name"
    ]
    
    func generateFileName(for session: RecordingSession) -> String {
        var fileName = template
        let dateFormatter = DateFormatter()
        
        // Replace template variables
        dateFormatter.dateFormat = dateFormat
        fileName = fileName.replacingOccurrences(of: "{date}", with: dateFormatter.string(from: session.startTime))
        
        dateFormatter.dateFormat = timeFormat
        fileName = fileName.replacingOccurrences(of: "{time}", with: dateFormatter.string(from: session.startTime))
        
        // Add prefix and suffix
        if !customPrefix.isEmpty {
            fileName = customPrefix + fileName
        }
        
        if !customSuffix.isEmpty {
            fileName = fileName + customSuffix
        }
        
        return fileName
    }
}
```

#### Directory Structure Settings
```swift
struct DirectorySettings {
    var baseOutputLocation: URL = FileManager.default.urls(for: .desktopDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first!
    var createSessionDirectories: Bool = true
    var organizeByDate: Bool = false
    var organizationStructure: OrganizationStructure = .flat
    
    enum OrganizationStructure: String, CaseIterable {
        case flat = "All files in one directory"
        case byType = "Separate folders for video/audio/data"
        case byDate = "Organize by recording date"
        case byProject = "Organize by project/tag"
        
        func createDirectoryStructure(at baseURL: URL, for session: RecordingSession) throws -> URL {
            switch self {
            case .flat:
                return baseURL
            case .byType:
                try createTypeBasedStructure(at: baseURL)
                return baseURL
            case .byDate:
                return try createDateBasedStructure(at: baseURL, for: session.startTime)
            case .byProject:
                return try createProjectBasedStructure(at: baseURL, project: session.projectName)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# 3. Core Features

## Screen Recording Engine

### High-Performance Video Capture

#### ScreenCaptureKit Integration
Did You Get It leverages Apple's latest ScreenCaptureKit framework for optimal performance:

```swift
// Core recording architecture
class CaptureSessionManager {
    private var stream: SCStream?
    private let videoProcessor: VideoProcessor
    private let audioProcessor: AudioProcessor
    
    func startCapture(configuration: CaptureConfiguration) async throws {
        // 60 FPS, full-resolution capture with minimal latency
        let streamConfig = SCStreamConfiguration()
        streamConfig.minimumFrameInterval = CMTime(value: 1, timescale: 60)
        streamConfig.pixelFormat = kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA
    }
}
```

#### Frame Rate Options
- **60 FPS**: Ultra-smooth recording for detailed demonstrations
- **30 FPS**: Balanced performance for most use cases
- **24 FPS**: Cinematic feel with lower resource usage
- **Variable FPS**: Adaptive frame rate based on content changes

#### Resolution Settings
- **Native Retina**: Full display resolution (e.g., 3024×1964 on MacBook Pro)
- **Scaled Retina**: 2x scaling for smaller files with excellent quality
- **Standard HD**: 1920×1080 for universal compatibility
- **Custom resolution**: User-defined output dimensions

### Recording Area Management

#### Full Screen Capture
```
Default Mode: Complete display capture
- Captures entire selected display
- Optimal performance for single-display setups
- Automatic handling of display changes
- Menu bar and dock included by default
```

#### Custom Area Selection
Interactive area selection with precision controls:

1. **Visual Selection Tool**
   - Drag to define recording rectangle
   - Real-time dimension display
   - Snap-to-window functionality
   - Grid alignment assistance

2. **Coordinate-Based Definition**
   ```json
   {
     "recording_area": {
       "x": 100,
       "y": 100,
       "width": 1200,
       "height": 800,
       "display_id": 1
     }
   }
   ```

3. **Window-Based Capture**
   - Select specific application windows
   - Follow window movement automatically
   - Exclude or include window shadows
   - Handle window resizing gracefully

#### Multi-Display Support

**Display Detection and Selection**
```swift
// Automatic display enumeration
let displays = SCShareableContent.displays
for display in displays {
    print("Display: \(display.displayID), Size: \(display.frame.size)")
}
```

**Recording Strategies**
- **Single display**: Record one display with full resources
- **Multi-display span**: Record across multiple displays as single canvas
- **Independent recording**: Separate recording streams per display
- **Display switching**: Change target display during recording

## Audio Recording System

### Multi-Source Audio Capture

#### System Audio Recording
Captures all system-generated audio with perfect synchronization:

```swift
class AudioProcessor {
    func captureSystemAudio() async throws {
        // Capture system audio through ScreenCaptureKit
        let filter = SCContentFilter(excludingApplications: [], 
                                   exceptingWindows: [])
        // Audio automatically synced with video stream
    }
}
```

**Features:**
- **Application-specific filtering**: Include/exclude specific app audio
- **System sounds**: Notifications, alerts, and UI sounds
- **Media playback**: Music, videos, and streaming audio
- **Perfect synchronization**: Frame-accurate audio-video alignment

#### Microphone Recording
High-quality microphone input with real-time monitoring:

- **Device selection**: Choose from all available audio input devices
- **Input level monitoring**: Real-time audio level visualization
- **Noise reduction**: Built-in audio processing filters
- **Sample rate options**: 44.1kHz, 48kHz, or 96kHz recording

#### Audio Mixing and Processing

**Real-Time Mixing**
```swift
// Mix multiple audio sources in real-time
let mixer = AVAudioMixerNode()
mixer.addInputWithFormat(systemAudioFormat, for: systemAudioBus)
mixer.addInputWithFormat(microphoneFormat, for: microphoneBus)
```

**Output Formats**
- **Separate tracks**: Individual files for each audio source
- **Mixed stereo**: Combined audio in single stereo track  
- **Multi-channel**: Preserve individual channels for post-processing
- **Lossless options**: FLAC, ALAC for professional use

**Audio Quality Settings**
```json
{
  "audio_settings": {
    "system_audio": {
      "enabled": true,
      "sample_rate": 48000,
      "bit_depth": 24,
      "format": "AAC"
    },
    "microphone": {
      "enabled": true,
      "device_id": "default",
      "gain": 0.8,
      "noise_reduction": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Input Tracking Engine

### Mouse Movement Tracking

#### High-Precision Movement Capture
```swift
class MouseTracker {
    func trackMouseEvents() {
        // Sub-pixel precision mouse tracking
        NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEventsMatching([.mouseMoved, .leftMouseDown, .rightMouseDown]) { event in
            let location = NSEvent.mouseLocation
            let timestamp = event.timestamp
            
            let mouseEvent = MouseEvent(
                x: location.x,
                y: location.y,
                timestamp: timestamp,
                type: event.type,
                precision: .subPixel
            )
        }
    }
}
```

**Tracking Capabilities**
- **Movement precision**: Sub-pixel accuracy for smooth playback
- **Click detection**: Left, right, and middle button events
- **Drag operations**: Start, continue, and end drag events
- **Scroll tracking**: Wheel and trackpad scroll events
- **Gesture recognition**: Multi-touch trackpad gestures

**Output Format**
```json
{
  "mouse_events": [
    {
      "timestamp": 1642261845.123456,
      "type": "move",
      "x": 1024.5,
      "y": 768.25,
      "screen_id": 1
    },
    {
      "timestamp": 1642261845.567890,
      "type": "click",
      "button": "left",
      "state": "down",
      "x": 1024.5,
      "y": 768.25
    }
  ]
}
```

### Keyboard Input Tracking

#### Comprehensive Keystroke Capture
```swift
class KeyboardTracker {
    func trackKeyboardEvents() {
        NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEventsMatching([.keyDown, .keyUp, .flagsChanged]) { event in
            let keyEvent = KeyboardEvent(
                keyCode: event.keyCode,
                characters: event.characters,
                modifiers: event.modifierFlags,
                timestamp: event.timestamp,
                eventType: event.type
            )
        }
    }
}
```

**Captured Data**
- **Key codes**: Raw key codes for accurate replay
- **Character representation**: Actual characters typed
- **Modifier states**: Cmd, Opt, Ctrl, Shift combinations
- **Timing precision**: Millisecond-accurate timestamps
- **Hold duration**: Key press and release timing

**Privacy Considerations**
```json
{
  "privacy_settings": {
    "capture_mode": "keys_only",  // "keys_only", "characters", "both"
    "exclude_passwords": true,
    "exclude_secure_fields": true,
    "anonymize_text": false
  }
}
```

### Event Correlation and Analysis

#### Cross-Device Event Matching
- **Temporal synchronization**: Match events across input devices
- **Action grouping**: Identify related events (drag operations, text selection)
- **Gesture recognition**: Detect common UI interaction patterns
- **Performance metrics**: Calculate interaction timing and efficiency

#### Data Export Formats

**JSON Output Structure**
```json
{
  "session_metadata": {
    "start_time": "2024-01-15T14:30:45.123Z",
    "end_time": "2024-01-15T14:35:22.456Z",
    "recording_area": {...},
    "system_info": {...}
  },
  "mouse_events": [...],
  "keyboard_events": [...],
  "system_events": [...]
}
```

**CSV Export for Analysis**
```csv
timestamp,event_type,device,x,y,key_code,characters,modifiers
1642261845.123,mouse_move,mouse,1024.5,768.25,,,
1642261845.567,key_down,keyboard,,,65,a,0
1642261845.890,key_up,keyboard,,,65,a,0
```

## Recording Session Management

### Session Configuration

#### Pre-Recording Setup
```swift
struct RecordingConfiguration {
    let recordingArea: RecordingArea
    let videoSettings: VideoSettings
    let audioSettings: AudioSettings
    let inputTracking: InputTrackingSettings
    let outputSettings: OutputSettings
}
```

#### Dynamic Configuration Changes
- **Area adjustment**: Modify recording area during session
- **Quality settings**: Change frame rate and resolution on-the-fly
- **Audio routing**: Switch audio sources during recording
- **Input sensitivity**: Adjust tracking precision while recording

### File Management

#### Output Organization
```
Output Directory Structure:
session_2024-01-15_14-30-45/
├── metadata.json          # Session configuration and info
├── video.mov             # Primary video recording
├── audio/
│   ├── system.wav        # System audio track
│   ├── microphone.wav    # Microphone audio track
│   └── mixed.wav         # Combined audio (if enabled)
├── input_data/
│   ├── mouse_events.json # Mouse interaction data
│   ├── keyboard_events.json # Keyboard input data
│   └── combined_events.json # Merged event timeline
└── thumbnails/
    ├── preview.jpg       # Session preview image
    └── timeline/         # Timeline thumbnail images
        ├── 00001.jpg
        ├── 00002.jpg
        └── ...
```

#### Automatic File Naming
```json
{
  "naming_template": "session_{date}_{time}",
  "date_format": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "time_format": "HH-mm-ss",
  "include_duration": true,
  "custom_prefix": "demo_"
}
```

### Performance Monitoring

#### Real-Time Metrics
- **Frame rate stability**: Monitor actual vs. target frame rate
- **Memory usage**: Track recording buffer and processing memory
- **Disk I/O**: Monitor write speeds and available storage
- **CPU utilization**: Balance quality with system performance

#### Quality Assurance
```swift
struct RecordingMetrics {
    let averageFrameRate: Double
    let droppedFrames: Int
    let audioBufferUnderruns: Int
    let memoryPeakUsage: UInt64
    let diskWriteSpeed: Double
}
```

# 9. Development & Contributing

## Development Environment Setup

### Prerequisites

```bash
# Install Xcode (latest version)

brew install git swift-format swiftlint xcbeautify
brew install --cask sf-symbols

brew install ffmpeg imagemagick jq
pip3 install pre-commit black isort
```

#### Swift and Xcode Setup
```bash
# Verify Swift version (should be 5.9+)

# Check Xcode version
xcodebuild -version

# Install Xcode command line tools
sudo xcode-select --switch /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
```

### Project Structure

#### Repository Organization
