#### Core Architecture Components
```swift
// Main architectural components overview
protocol RecordingServiceProtocol {
    func startRecording(with configuration: RecordingConfiguration) async throws
    func stopRecording() async throws
    var isRecording: Bool { get }
}

// Dependency injection container
class ServiceContainer {
    static let shared = ServiceContainer()
    
    // Core services
    lazy var recordingManager: RecordingServiceProtocol = RecordingManager()
    lazy var audioProcessor: AudioProcessorProtocol = AudioProcessor()
    lazy var inputTracker: InputTrackerProtocol = InputTracker()
    lazy var fileManager: OutputFileManagerProtocol = OutputFileManager()
}

// Protocol-oriented design for testability
protocol VideoProcessorProtocol: Actor {
    func processFrame(_ imageBuffer: CVImageBuffer, timestamp: CMTime) async
    func configureEncoder(settings: VideoSettings) async throws
}
```

### Building from Source

#### Build Process
```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/twardoch/didyougetit-mac.git
cd didyougetit-mac

# Install pre-commit hooks
pre-commit install

# Build using Makefile
make build

# Or build with Xcode
xcodebuild -project DidYouGet.xcodeproj -scheme DidYouGet -configuration Release

# Run the application
./run.sh

# Build for distribution
make build-release
```

#### Build Configuration
```swift
// Build configurations in project settings
#if DEBUG
    let logLevel: Logger.Level = .debug
    let enablePerformanceMetrics = true
    let skipPermissionChecks = false
#else
    let logLevel: Logger.Level = .info
    let enablePerformanceMetrics = false
    let skipPermissionChecks = false
#endif

// Feature flags for development
struct FeatureFlags {
    static let experimentalAudioProcessing = false
    static let advancedInputTracking = true
    static let mlGestureRecognition = false
}
```

#### Makefile Targets
```makefile
# Available make targets
.PHONY: build test clean install format lint

build:
	xcodebuild -project DidYouGet.xcodeproj -scheme DidYouGet -configuration Debug

build-release:
	xcodebuild -project DidYouGet.xcodeproj -scheme DidYouGet -configuration Release -archivePath build/DidYouGet.xcarchive archive

test:
	xcodebuild test -project DidYouGet.xcodeproj -scheme DidYouGet -destination 'platform=macOS'

clean:
	xcodebuild clean -project DidYouGet.xcodeproj -scheme DidYouGet
	rm -rf build/

format:
	swift-format --in-place --recursive Sources/ Tests/

lint:
	swiftlint --config .swiftlint.yml

install: build-release
	cp -R build/DidYouGet.xcarchive/Products/Applications/DidYouGet.app /Applications/
```

## Testing Framework

### Unit Testing Structure

#### Test Organization
```swift
// Example unit test structure
import XCTest
@testable import DidYouGet

class RecordingManagerTests: XCTestCase {
    var recordingManager: RecordingManager!
    var mockAudioProcessor: MockAudioProcessor!
    var mockVideoProcessor: MockVideoProcessor!
    
    override func setUp() {
        super.setUp()
        mockAudioProcessor = MockAudioProcessor()
        mockVideoProcessor = MockVideoProcessor()
        recordingManager = RecordingManager(
            audioProcessor: mockAudioProcessor,
            videoProcessor: mockVideoProcessor
        )
    }
    
    override func tearDown() {
        recordingManager = nil
        mockAudioProcessor = nil
        mockVideoProcessor = nil
        super.tearDown()
    }
    
    func testStartRecording() async throws {
        // Given
        let configuration = RecordingConfiguration.defaultConfiguration
        
        // When
        try await recordingManager.startRecording(with: configuration)
        
        // Then
        XCTAssertTrue(recordingManager.isRecording)
        XCTAssertTrue(mockAudioProcessor.didStartProcessing)
        XCTAssertTrue(mockVideoProcessor.didStartProcessing)
    }
}
```

#### Mock Objects for Testing
```swift
// Mock implementations for testing
class MockAudioProcessor: AudioProcessorProtocol {
    var didStartProcessing = false
    var didStopProcessing = false
    var processedSamples: [CMSampleBuffer] = []
    
    func startProcessing(configuration: AudioConfiguration) async throws {
        didStartProcessing = true
    }
    
    func stopProcessing() async throws {
        didStopProcessing = true
    }
    
    func processAudioSample(_ sampleBuffer: CMSampleBuffer) async {
        processedSamples.append(sampleBuffer)
    }
}

class MockRecordingService: RecordingServiceProtocol {
    var isRecording = false
    var startRecordingCalled = false
    var stopRecordingCalled = false
    var lastConfiguration: RecordingConfiguration?
    
    func startRecording(with configuration: RecordingConfiguration) async throws {
        startRecordingCalled = true
        lastConfiguration = configuration
        isRecording = true
    }
    
    func stopRecording() async throws {
        stopRecordingCalled = true
        isRecording = false
    }
}
```

### Integration Testing

#### UI Testing with XCTest
```swift
import XCTest

class DidYouGetUITests: XCTestCase {
    var app: XCUIApplication!
    
    override func setUp() {
        super.setUp()
        continueAfterFailure = false
        app = XCUIApplication()
        
        // Configure app for testing
        app.launchEnvironment["UITEST_MODE"] = "1"
        app.launchEnvironment["SKIP_PERMISSIONS"] = "1"
        app.launch()
    }
    
    func testRecordingWorkflow() throws {
        // Test complete recording workflow
        let recordButton = app.buttons["Record"]
        XCTAssertTrue(recordButton.exists)
        
        // Start recording
        recordButton.tap()
        
        // Verify recording indicator appears
        let recordingIndicator = app.staticTexts["Recording"]
        XCTAssertTrue(recordingIndicator.waitForExistence(timeout: 2.0))
        
        // Wait a moment then stop
        sleep(3)
        recordButton.tap()
        
        // Verify recording stopped
        XCTAssertFalse(recordingIndicator.exists)
        
        // Check that files were created
        // This would require additional helper functions to verify file system
    }
    
    func testPreferencesConfiguration() throws {
        // Open preferences
        app.menuBarItems["Did You Get It"].click()
        app.menuItems["Preferences"].click()
        
        let preferencesWindow = app.windows["Preferences"]
        XCTAssertTrue(preferencesWindow.waitForExistence(timeout: 2.0))
        
        // Test frame rate selection
        let frameRatePopup = preferencesWindow.popUpButtons["Frame Rate"]
        frameRatePopup.click()
        frameRatePopup.menuItems["30 FPS"].click()
        
        // Verify setting was saved
        XCTAssertEqual(frameRatePopup.value as? String, "30 FPS")
    }
}
```

#### Performance Testing
```swift
class PerformanceTests: XCTestCase {
    func testRecordingPerformance() throws {
        let recordingManager = RecordingManager()
        let configuration = RecordingConfiguration.defaultConfiguration
        
        measure(metrics: [XCTCPUMetric(), XCTMemoryMetric()]) {
            let expectation = XCTestExpectation(description: "Recording completes")
            
            Task {
                do {
                    try await recordingManager.startRecording(with: configuration)
                    try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 5_000_000_000) // 5 seconds
                    try await recordingManager.stopRecording()
                    expectation.fulfill()
                } catch {
                    XCTFail("Recording failed: \(error)")
                }
            }
            
            wait(for: [expectation], timeout: 10.0)
        }
    }
    
    func testFrameProcessingPerformance() throws {
        let videoProcessor = VideoProcessor()
        let testImageBuffer = createTestImageBuffer()
        
        measure {
            Task {
                for i in 0..<100 {
                    let timestamp = CMTime(value: Int64(i), timescale: 60)
                    await videoProcessor.processFrame(testImageBuffer, timestamp: timestamp)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Code Quality and Standards

### Coding Standards

#### Swift Style Guide
```swift
// Follow Swift API Design Guidelines and project-specific standards

// MARK: - Good Examples

// Protocol naming: use -able, -ible suffixes or descriptive nouns
protocol Recordable {
    func startRecording() async throws
}

protocol RecordingDelegate: AnyObject {
    func recordingDidStart()
    func recordingDidStop(withFiles files: [URL])
}

// Type naming: Use clear, descriptive names
struct RecordingConfiguration {
    let frameRate: Int
    let resolution: Resolution
    let audioSettings: AudioSettings
}

// Function naming: Start with verb, be descriptive
func startRecording(with configuration: RecordingConfiguration) async throws {
    // Implementation
}

// Variable naming: Use descriptive names, avoid abbreviations
private var recordingDuration: TimeInterval = 0
private var isCurrentlyRecording = false

// MARK: - Code Organization

class RecordingManager {
    // MARK: - Properties
    private let audioProcessor: AudioProcessorProtocol
    private let videoProcessor: VideoProcessorProtocol
    
    // MARK: - Initialization
    init(audioProcessor: AudioProcessorProtocol, videoProcessor: VideoProcessorProtocol) {
        self.audioProcessor = audioProcessor
        self.videoProcessor = videoProcessor
    }
    
    // MARK: - Public Methods
    func startRecording(with configuration: RecordingConfiguration) async throws {
        // Implementation
    }
    
    // MARK: - Private Methods
    private func configureRecordingSession() {
        // Implementation
    }
}
```

#### Documentation Standards
```swift
/// Manages video recording sessions with high-performance capture and processing.
///
/// The `RecordingManager` coordinates between video capture, audio processing, and input tracking
/// to create comprehensive recording sessions. It provides async/await APIs for all recording
/// operations and maintains thread safety through Swift's actor model.
///
/// Example usage:
/// ```swift
/// let manager = RecordingManager()
/// let config = RecordingConfiguration(frameRate: 60, resolution: .native)
/// try await manager.startRecording(with: config)
/// // ... perform actions to record
/// try await manager.stopRecording()
/// ```
class RecordingManager {
    
    /// Starts a new recording session with the specified configuration.
    ///
    /// - Parameter configuration: The recording configuration including video settings,
    ///   audio settings, and input tracking options.
    /// - Throws: `RecordingError.permissionDenied` if required permissions are not granted.
    /// - Throws: `RecordingError.insufficientDiskSpace` if there's not enough storage.
    /// - Throws: `RecordingError.alreadyRecording` if a recording session is already active.
    func startRecording(with configuration: RecordingConfiguration) async throws {
        // Implementation
    }
}
```

### Code Review Process

#### Pre-Commit Hooks
```bash
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: swift-format
        name: swift-format
        entry: swift-format
        language: system
        args: [--in-place]
        files: \.swift$
        
      - id: swiftlint
        name: SwiftLint
        entry: swiftlint
        language: system
        args: [--strict]
        files: \.swift$
        
      - id: tests
        name: Run Tests
        entry: make test
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
        always_run: true
```

#### Code Review Checklist
- [ ] **Functionality**: Does the code work as intended?
- [ ] **Performance**: Are there any performance implications?
- [ ] **Memory Management**: Proper memory management and no leaks?
- [ ] **Thread Safety**: Proper use of actors/async-await for concurrency?
- [ ] **Error Handling**: Comprehensive error handling with meaningful messages?
- [ ] **Testing**: Adequate unit test coverage for new functionality?
- [ ] **Documentation**: Clear documentation for public APIs?
- [ ] **Style**: Follows project coding standards and Swift conventions?

## Contributing Guidelines

### Getting Started with Contributions

#### First-Time Contributors
1. **Fork the repository** on GitHub
2. **Clone your fork** locally:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-username/didyougetit-mac.git
cd didyougetit-mac
```

3. **Set up the development environment**:
```bash
make setup-dev
```

4. **Create a feature branch**:
```bash
git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
```

5. **Make your changes** following the coding standards
6. **Run tests** to ensure nothing is broken:
```bash
make test
```

7. **Commit your changes** with descriptive messages:
```bash
git commit -m "feat: add support for custom recording areas

- Implement interactive area selection
- Add coordinate validation
- Update UI for area configuration
- Add unit tests for area selection logic"
```

#### Contribution Types

**Bug Fixes:**
- Include steps to reproduce the bug
- Add regression tests
- Update documentation if needed

**New Features:**
- Discuss the feature in an issue first
- Include comprehensive tests
- Update documentation and examples
- Consider performance implications

**Documentation:**
- Fix typos and improve clarity
- Add examples and use cases
- Update API documentation
- Improve setup instructions

### Pull Request Process

#### PR Template
```markdown
## Description
Brief description of changes and motivation.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that causes existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Testing
- [ ] Unit tests pass
- [ ] Integration tests pass
- [ ] Manual testing completed
- [ ] Performance impact assessed

## Screenshots/Recordings
Include screenshots or recordings demonstrating the changes (if applicable).

## Checklist
- [ ] Code follows project style guidelines
- [ ] Self-review completed
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [ ] Tests added/updated
- [ ] No breaking changes (or marked as breaking)
```

#### Review Process
1. **Automated Checks**: CI/CD pipeline runs tests and linting
2. **Code Review**: At least one maintainer reviews the code
3. **Testing**: Manual testing by reviewers if needed
4. **Documentation**: Verify documentation is updated
5. **Approval**: PR approved by maintainer
6. **Merge**: Squash and merge to main branch

### Development Workflow

#### Git Workflow
```bash
# Keep your fork updated
git remote add upstream https://github.com/twardoch/didyougetit-mac.git
git fetch upstream
git checkout main
git merge upstream/main

# Create feature branch
git checkout -b feature/new-audio-filter

# Make changes and commit
git add .
git commit -m "feat: implement noise reduction audio filter"

# Push to your fork
git push origin feature/new-audio-filter

# Create pull request on GitHub
```

#### Continuous Integration

#### GitHub Actions Workflow
```yaml
name: CI/CD Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, develop ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Setup Xcode
      uses: maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1
      with:
        xcode-version: latest-stable
    
    - name: Cache Swift packages
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: .build
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-spm-${{ hashFiles('Package.swift') }}
    
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        brew install swiftlint swift-format
    
    - name: Lint code
      run: swiftlint --strict
    
    - name: Format check
      run: swift-format --lint --recursive Sources/ Tests/
    
    - name: Build
      run: make build
    
    - name: Run tests
      run: make test
    
    - name: Build release
      if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      run: make build-release
    
    - name: Upload artifacts
      if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: DidYouGetIt-Release
        path: build/DidYouGet.app
```

### Release Process

#### Version Management
```swift
// Version.swift - Centralized version management
struct AppVersion {
    static let major = 1
    static let minor = 0
    static let patch = 0
    static let build = 1
    
    static var versionString: String {
        return "\(major).\(minor).\(patch)"
    }
    
    static var fullVersionString: String {
        return "\(versionString) (\(build))"
    }
}
```

#### Release Checklist
- [ ] All tests passing
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [ ] Version number incremented
- [ ] Changelog updated
- [ ] Performance benchmarks run
- [ ] Manual testing on different macOS versions
- [ ] Code signing and notarization completed
- [ ] Release notes prepared

#### Automated Release
```bash
# scripts/release.sh
#!/bin/bash

set -e

VERSION=$1
if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <version>"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Preparing release $VERSION..."

# Update version in code
sed -i '' "s/static let patch = .*/static let patch = ${VERSION##*.}/" Sources/DidYouGet/Version.swift

# Build release
make build-release

# Create release archive
cd build
zip -r "DidYouGetIt-${VERSION}.zip" DidYouGet.app

# Create GitHub release
gh release create "v${VERSION}" \
    "DidYouGetIt-${VERSION}.zip" \
    --title "Did You Get It v${VERSION}" \
    --notes-file ../CHANGELOG.md
```

This completes the comprehensive 9-chapter documentation for Did You Get It. The documentation covers everything from basic usage to advanced development topics, providing users and contributors with complete information about the application.

# 2. Getting Started

## Installation

### Download Options

#### Official Release (Recommended)
1. Visit [https://didyouget.it](https://didyouget.it)
2. Download the latest `.dmg` file
3. Open the downloaded file and drag "Did You Get It" to Applications
4. Launch from Applications folder or Spotlight

#### Build from Source
```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/twardoch/didyougetit-mac.git
cd didyougetit-mac

# Build and run
make build
./run.sh
```

### First Launch Setup

#### Required Permissions
On first launch, macOS will request several permissions:

1. **Screen Recording Permission**
   - Essential for video capture functionality
   - Go to System Preferences → Security & Privacy → Privacy → Screen Recording
   - Check the box next to "Did You Get It"

2. **Microphone Permission** (if audio recording enabled)
   - Required for microphone input
   - Go to System Preferences → Security & Privacy → Privacy → Microphone
   - Check the box next to "Did You Get It"

3. **Accessibility Permission** (for input tracking)
   - Needed for mouse and keyboard tracking
   - Go to System Preferences → Security & Privacy → Privacy → Accessibility
   - Check the box next to "Did You Get It"

#### Initial Configuration
The app will open with default settings optimized for most users:
- **Recording area**: Full screen of primary display
- **Frame rate**: 60 FPS
- **Audio**: System audio enabled, microphone disabled
- **Input tracking**: Mouse and keyboard tracking enabled
- **Output location**: Desktop folder

## Quick Start Guide

### Your First Recording

1. **Launch the app**
   ```
   Open Did You Get It from Applications or press Cmd+Space and type "Did You Get It"
   ```

2. **Check recording area**
   - The app will highlight the recording area with a subtle overlay
   - Default is full screen of your primary display

3. **Start recording**
   - Press the **Record** button or use keyboard shortcut `Cmd+R`
   - The interface will minimize to avoid recording UI elements

4. **Perform your actions**
   - Do whatever you want to record
   - Mouse movements and keyboard input are being tracked automatically

5. **Stop recording**
   - Press `Cmd+R` again or click the stop button in the menu bar
   - Files will be saved automatically to your configured location

### Understanding Output Files

After recording, you'll find these files in your output directory:

```
recording_2024-01-15_14-30-45/
├── video.mov           # Main video recording
├── audio.wav           # Audio track (if recorded separately)
├── mouse_events.json   # Mouse movement and click data
├── keyboard_events.json # Keyboard input data
└── metadata.json       # Recording session information
```

### Basic Keyboard Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `Cmd+R` | Start/Stop recording |
| `Cmd+P` | Open Preferences |
| `Cmd+Q` | Quit application |
| `Cmd+,` | Open Settings |
| `Esc` | Cancel current recording |

## Essential Settings

### Recording Area Configuration

#### Full Screen Recording
- **Default setting**: Captures entire primary display
- **Best for**: General screen recording, tutorials
- **Performance**: Optimal for single-display setups

#### Custom Area Selection
1. Open Preferences (`Cmd+,`)
2. Select "Custom Area" from Recording Area dropdown
3. Click "Select Area" button
4. Drag to define the recording rectangle
5. Click "Confirm Selection"

#### Multi-Display Setup
- **Display selection**: Choose specific display from dropdown
- **Area per display**: Define custom areas on each display
- **Performance note**: Recording multiple displays increases resource usage

### Audio Configuration

#### System Audio Recording
```
Settings → Audio → System Audio: Enabled
```
- Captures all system sounds (music, notifications, app audio)
- Uses ScreenCaptureKit's audio capture for synchronization

#### Microphone Recording
```
Settings → Audio → Microphone: Choose device
```
- Select from available microphone devices
- Adjust input levels with built-in level meter
- Real-time audio monitoring available

#### Audio Mixing Options
- **Separate tracks**: Save system and mic audio as separate files
- **Mixed output**: Combine into single audio track
- **Audio-only mode**: Record audio without video

### Input Tracking Settings

#### Precision Levels
- **High precision**: Sub-pixel mouse movement tracking
- **Standard precision**: Pixel-level accuracy (recommended)
- **Low precision**: Reduced data volume for long recordings

#### Event Filtering
- **All events**: Capture every mouse movement and key press
- **Significant events only**: Filter minor movements and key repeats
- **Clicks and keys only**: Record only deliberate actions

## First Recording Walkthrough

Let's create your first recording with optimal settings:

### Step 1: Prepare Your Workspace

# Create a dedicated folder for your recordings
mkdir ~/Desktop/DidYouGetIt-Recordings

1. Open Did You Get It
2. Press `Cmd+,` to open preferences

   - **Video**: 60 FPS, Full Quality
   - **Audio**: System Audio enabled
   - **Input Tracking**: Mouse and Keyboard enabled
   - **Recording Area**: Full Screen

2. Open a few applications
3. Type some text
4. Move mouse around
5. Press `Cmd+R` to stop

Navigate to your recordings folder and examine:
- **Video quality**: Smooth 60 FPS playback
- **Audio sync**: Perfect audio-video synchronization
- **Input data**: JSON files with precise timing data

## Performance Optimization

### For Best Results
- **Close unnecessary applications** before recording
- **Use SSD storage** for recording output
- **Monitor CPU and memory usage** in Activity Monitor
- **Record to local storage** rather than network drives

### Resource Management
```
Recommended settings for different scenarios:

Tutorials/Demos:
- 30 FPS video
- Standard input precision
- System audio enabled

Development/Debugging:
- 60 FPS video
- High input precision
- Separate audio tracks

Long-form Recording:
- 24 FPS video
- Low input precision
- Compressed output formats
```

## Troubleshooting First Launch

### Common Issues

#### "App cannot be opened" error
```bash
# Remove quarantine attribute
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Did\ You\ Get\ It.app
```

#### Recording area not visible
1. Check Screen Recording permission in System Preferences
2. Restart the application after granting permission
3. Verify display settings aren't interfering

#### No audio in recordings
1. Verify microphone/system audio permissions
2. Check audio device selection in preferences
3. Test audio levels before recording

#### Performance issues
1. Close resource-intensive applications
2. Lower recording quality settings
3. Record to faster storage device

### Getting Help
- **Check logs**: `~/Library/Logs/DidYouGetIt/`
- **Reset preferences**: Delete `~/Library/Preferences/it.didyouget.mac.plist`
- **GitHub issues**: Report bugs and request features

# 1. Introduction

## What is Did You Get It?

Did You Get It is a high-performance macOS screen recording application designed for users who need professional-quality recordings with minimal system overhead and maximum flexibility. Built with Swift and SwiftUI, it leverages Apple's latest ScreenCaptureKit framework to deliver 60 FPS, full-resolution (Retina) video capture alongside comprehensive input tracking capabilities.

## Key Design Principles

### Performance First
- **Zero-compromise quality**: Native 60 FPS recording at full Retina resolution
- **Minimal system impact**: Optimized memory usage and CPU efficiency
- **Real-time processing**: Live audio mixing and input tracking without bottlenecks

### Minimal, Purposeful Interface
- **Extreme simplicity**: Only essential controls visible
- **Keyboard-driven workflow**: Minimal mouse interaction required
- **Distraction-free recording**: UI gets out of your way when recording

### Developer-Friendly Output
- **Structured data formats**: JSON for input tracking data
- **Flexible file organization**: Configurable output locations and naming
- **Integration-ready**: Designed for workflow automation and scripting

## What Makes It Different?

### Comprehensive Input Tracking
Unlike basic screen recorders that only capture video, Did You Get It simultaneously records:
- **Mouse movements** with pixel-perfect accuracy
- **Click events** with press/release timing
- **Keyboard input** with precise keystroke timing
- **All data in structured JSON format**

### Professional Audio Handling
- **Multi-source recording**: System audio, microphone, or both
- **Real-time mixing**: Combine multiple audio sources seamlessly
- **High-quality output**: Lossless audio capture options

### Configurable Recording Areas
- **Multi-display support**: Record from any connected display
- **Custom regions**: Define specific screen areas to capture
- **Dynamic adjustment**: Change recording parameters without stopping

## Use Cases

### Software Development & Demos
- **Bug reproduction**: Capture exact user interactions for debugging
- **Feature demonstrations**: Show new functionality with context
- **Tutorial creation**: Record step-by-step processes with input data

### UX Research & Testing
- **User session recording**: Capture complete user interactions
- **Usability analysis**: Review mouse patterns and keyboard usage
- **Performance testing**: Monitor system behavior during tasks

### Content Creation
- **Educational content**: Create detailed tutorials and walkthroughs
- **Product showcases**: Professional-quality demonstrations
- **Training materials**: Comprehensive learning resources

### Workflow Automation
- **Process documentation**: Record and analyze repetitive tasks
- **Automation scripting**: Use input data to create automation scripts
- **Quality assurance**: Validate user interface interactions

## System Requirements

### macOS Version Support
- **Minimum**: macOS 13.0 (Ventura)
- **Recommended**: macOS 14.0 (Sonoma) or later
- **Framework dependencies**: ScreenCaptureKit, AVFoundation, SwiftUI

### Hardware Requirements
- **Memory**: 8GB RAM minimum, 16GB recommended for 4K recording
- **Storage**: SSD recommended for high-framerate recording
- **Display**: Any Mac with Retina display support

### Permissions Required
- **Screen Recording**: Essential for video capture functionality
- **Microphone Access**: Required for audio recording (if enabled)
- **Accessibility**: Needed for comprehensive input tracking

## Privacy & Security

### Data Handling
- **Local processing only**: No cloud uploads or external data transmission
- **User-controlled storage**: All recordings saved to user-specified locations
- **Transparent permissions**: Clear explanation of required system access

### Security Considerations
- **Sandboxed execution**: Runs within macOS security boundaries
- **Minimal permissions**: Requests only necessary system access
- **Code signing**: Verified developer identity and integrity

## Getting Help

### Documentation Resources
- **Complete user guide**: Step-by-step instructions for all features
- **Developer documentation**: Architecture and API reference
- **Troubleshooting guide**: Solutions for common issues

### Community & Support
- **GitHub repository**: Source code, issues, and discussions
- **Feature requests**: Community-driven development priorities
- **Bug reports**: Collaborative issue resolution

Ready to get started? Continue to [Getting Started](getting-started.md) for installation and setup instructions.

# 5. Technical Architecture

## System Overview

### Architecture Principles

#### Protocol-Oriented Design
Did You Get It is built using Swift's protocol-oriented programming paradigm for maximum flexibility and testability:

```swift
// Core recording protocol defines the interface
protocol RecordingServiceProtocol {
    func startRecording(with configuration: RecordingConfiguration) async throws
    func stopRecording() async throws
    func pauseRecording() async throws
    func resumeRecording() async throws
    var isRecording: Bool { get }
    var currentConfiguration: RecordingConfiguration? { get }
}

// Concrete implementation with async/await
class RecordingManager: RecordingServiceProtocol {
    private let captureSession: CaptureSessionManager
    private let audioProcessor: AudioProcessor
    private let inputTracker: InputTracker
    
    // Implementation uses modern Swift concurrency
}
```

#### Async/Await Concurrency Model
All recording operations use Swift's modern concurrency features:

```swift
// Non-blocking recording operations
actor RecordingSession {
    private var isActive = false
    private var recordingTask: Task<Void, Error>?
    
    func start() async throws {
        guard !isActive else { return }
        
        recordingTask = Task {
            try await performRecording()
        }
        
        isActive = true
    }
    
    private func performRecording() async throws {
        // Concurrent processing of video, audio, and input streams
        async let videoStream = processVideoFrames()
        async let audioStream = processAudioSamples()
        async let inputEvents = processInputEvents()
        
        try await (videoStream, audioStream, inputEvents)
    }
}
```

#### Dependency Injection Architecture
Clean separation of concerns through dependency injection:

```swift
// Service container for dependency management
class ServiceContainer {
    static let shared = ServiceContainer()
    
    lazy var recordingManager: RecordingServiceProtocol = {
        RecordingManager(
            captureSession: captureSessionManager,
            audioProcessor: audioProcessor,
            inputTracker: inputTracker,
            fileManager: outputFileManager
        )
    }()
    
    lazy var captureSessionManager: CaptureSessionManager = {
        CaptureSessionManager(logger: logger)
    }()
}
```

## Core Components

### Recording Manager

#### Singleton Pattern with Protocol Interface
```swift
// Thread-safe singleton with protocol conformance
final class RecordingManager: ObservableObject, RecordingServiceProtocol {
    static let shared = RecordingManager()
    
    @Published private(set) var isRecording = false
    @Published private(set) var recordingDuration: TimeInterval = 0
    @Published private(set) var currentStatus: RecordingStatus = .idle
    
    private let captureSession: CaptureSessionManager
    private let audioProcessor: AudioProcessorProtocol
    private let inputTracker: InputTrackerProtocol
    private let outputManager: OutputFileManagerProtocol
    
    private init() {
        // Initialize dependencies
        self.captureSession = CaptureSessionManager()
        self.audioProcessor = AudioProcessor()
        self.inputTracker = InputTracker()
        self.outputManager = OutputFileManager()
        
        setupRecordingPipeline()
    }
}
```

#### State Management
```swift
enum RecordingStatus {
    case idle
    case preparing
    case recording(startTime: Date)
    case paused(pauseTime: Date)
    case stopping
    case processing
    case error(RecordingError)
}

struct RecordingConfiguration {
    let videoSettings: VideoSettings
    let audioSettings: AudioSettings
    let inputTrackingSettings: InputTrackingSettings
    let outputSettings: OutputSettings
    let recordingArea: RecordingArea
}
```

### Capture Session Manager

#### ScreenCaptureKit Integration
```swift
import ScreenCaptureKit

class CaptureSessionManager: NSObject {
    private var stream: SCStream?
    private var streamOutput: SCStreamFrameOutput?
    private let logger: Logger
    
    func startCapture(configuration: RecordingConfiguration) async throws {
        // Get shareable content
        let content = try await SCShareableContent.excludingDesktopWindows(false, onScreenWindowsOnly: true)
        
        // Create content filter
        let filter = SCContentFilter(display: configuration.display, excludingWindows: [])
        
        // Configure stream
        let streamConfig = SCStreamConfiguration()
        streamConfig.width = configuration.resolution.width
        streamConfig.height = configuration.resolution.height
        streamConfig.minimumFrameInterval = CMTime(value: 1, timescale: Int32(configuration.frameRate))
        streamConfig.pixelFormat = kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA
        streamConfig.showsCursor = configuration.showCursor
        
        // Create and start stream
        stream = SCStream(filter: filter, configuration: streamConfig, delegate: self)
        try await stream?.startCapture(with: streamOutput)
    }
}
```

#### Frame Processing Pipeline
```swift
extension CaptureSessionManager: SCStreamDelegate, SCStreamOutput {
    func stream(_ stream: SCStream, didOutputSampleBuffer sampleBuffer: CMSampleBuffer, of type: SCStreamOutputType) {
        switch type {
        case .screen:
            Task { await processVideoFrame(sampleBuffer) }
        case .audio:
            Task { await processAudioSample(sampleBuffer) }
        @unknown default:
            logger.warning("Unknown stream output type: \(type)")
        }
    }
    
    private func processVideoFrame(_ sampleBuffer: CMSampleBuffer) async {
        guard let imageBuffer = CMSampleBufferGetImageBuffer(sampleBuffer) else { return }
        
        // Process frame with video processor
        await videoProcessor.processFrame(imageBuffer, timestamp: CMSampleBufferGetPresentationTimeStamp(sampleBuffer))
    }
}
```

### Video Processing System

#### Video Processor Protocol
```swift
protocol VideoProcessorProtocol: Actor {
    func processFrame(_ imageBuffer: CVImageBuffer, timestamp: CMTime) async
    func configureEncoder(settings: VideoSettings) async throws
    func finishEncoding() async throws -> URL
}

actor VideoProcessor: VideoProcessorProtocol {
    private var writer: AVAssetWriter?
    private var videoInput: AVAssetWriterInput?
    private var adaptor: AVAssetWriterInputPixelBufferAdaptor?
    private let processingQueue: DispatchQueue
    
    func processFrame(_ imageBuffer: CVImageBuffer, timestamp: CMTime) async {
        guard let videoInput = videoInput,
              let adaptor = adaptor,
              videoInput.isReadyForMoreMediaData else { return }
        
        // Append frame to video stream
        adaptor.append(imageBuffer, withPresentationTime: timestamp)
    }
}
```

#### Encoding Configuration
```swift
struct VideoSettings {
    let codec: AVVideoCodecType
    let width: Int
    let height: Int
    let frameRate: Int
    let bitRate: Int
    let keyFrameInterval: Int
    
    var compressionProperties: [String: Any] {
        return [
            AVVideoAverageBitRateKey: bitRate,
            AVVideoMaxKeyFrameIntervalKey: keyFrameInterval,
            AVVideoProfileLevelKey: AVVideoProfileLevelH264HighAutoLevel
        ]
    }
}
```

### Audio Processing System

#### Multi-Source Audio Handling
```swift
protocol AudioProcessorProtocol: Actor {
    func startProcessing(configuration: AudioConfiguration) async throws
    func processSystemAudio(_ sampleBuffer: CMSampleBuffer) async
    func processMicrophoneAudio(_ sampleBuffer: CMSampleBuffer) async
    func finishProcessing() async throws -> [URL]
}

actor AudioProcessor: AudioProcessorProtocol {
    private var systemAudioWriter: AVAssetWriter?
    private var microphoneAudioWriter: AVAssetWriter?
    private var mixedAudioWriter: AVAssetWriter?
    
    func processSystemAudio(_ sampleBuffer: CMSampleBuffer) async {
        // Write to system audio track
        await writeAudioSample(sampleBuffer, to: systemAudioWriter)
        
        // Mix with microphone if enabled
        if configuration.shouldMixAudio {
            await mixAudioSample(sampleBuffer, source: .system)
        }
    }
}
```

#### Audio Format Management
```swift
struct AudioConfiguration {
    let systemAudioEnabled: Bool
    let microphoneEnabled: Bool
    let shouldMixAudio: Bool
    let sampleRate: Double
    let channelCount: Int
    let bitDepth: Int
    
    var formatDescription: AudioStreamBasicDescription {
        AudioStreamBasicDescription(
            mSampleRate: sampleRate,
            mFormatID: kAudioFormatLinearPCM,
            mFormatFlags: kAudioFormatFlagIsFloat | kAudioFormatFlagIsPacked,
            mBytesPerPacket: UInt32(channelCount * MemoryLayout<Float32>.size),
            mFramesPerPacket: 1,
            mBytesPerFrame: UInt32(channelCount * MemoryLayout<Float32>.size),
            mChannelsPerFrame: UInt32(channelCount),
            mBitsPerChannel: UInt32(bitDepth),
            mReserved: 0
        )
    }
}
```

### Input Tracking System

#### Event Monitoring Architecture
```swift
protocol InputTrackerProtocol {
    func startTracking(configuration: InputTrackingConfiguration) throws
    func stopTracking() throws
    var mouseEvents: AsyncStream<MouseEvent> { get }
    var keyboardEvents: AsyncStream<KeyboardEvent> { get }
}

class InputTracker: InputTrackerProtocol {
    private var mouseMonitor: Any?
    private var keyboardMonitor: Any?
    private let eventProcessor: InputEventProcessor
    
    func startTracking(configuration: InputTrackingConfiguration) throws {
        // Start mouse event monitoring
        mouseMonitor = NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEventsMatching([
            .mouseMoved, .leftMouseDown, .leftMouseUp, .rightMouseDown, .rightMouseUp, .scrollWheel
        ]) { [weak self] event in
            Task { await self?.processMouseEvent(event) }
        }
        
        // Start keyboard event monitoring
        keyboardMonitor = NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEventsMatching([
            .keyDown, .keyUp, .flagsChanged
        ]) { [weak self] event in
            Task { await self?.processKeyboardEvent(event) }
        }
    }
}
```

#### Event Data Models
```swift
struct MouseEvent: Codable, Identifiable {
    let id = UUID()
    let timestamp: TimeInterval
    let type: MouseEventType
    let location: CGPoint
    let buttonState: MouseButtonState?
    let scrollDelta: CGPoint?
    let clickCount: Int?
    
    enum MouseEventType: String, Codable {
        case move, click, scroll, drag
    }
    
    enum MouseButtonState: String, Codable {
        case down, up
    }
}

struct KeyboardEvent: Codable, Identifiable {
    let id = UUID()
    let timestamp: TimeInterval
    let type: KeyboardEventType
    let keyCode: UInt16
    let characters: String?
    let modifierFlags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags
    
    enum KeyboardEventType: String, Codable {
        case keyDown, keyUp, flagsChanged
    }
}
```

### File Management System

#### Output File Manager
```swift
protocol OutputFileManagerProtocol {
    func prepareOutputDirectory(for session: RecordingSession) async throws -> URL
    func saveVideoFile(_ data: Data, to directory: URL) async throws -> URL
    func saveAudioFiles(_ audioData: [AudioTrack], to directory: URL) async throws -> [URL]
    func saveInputData(_ events: InputEventCollection, to directory: URL) async throws -> URL
}

class OutputFileManager: OutputFileManagerProtocol {
    private let fileManager = FileManager.default
    private let sessionFormatter: SessionNameFormatter
    
    func prepareOutputDirectory(for session: RecordingSession) async throws -> URL {
        let baseURL = session.configuration.outputLocation
        let sessionName = sessionFormatter.formatName(for: session)
        let sessionURL = baseURL.appendingPathComponent(sessionName)
        
        try fileManager.createDirectory(at: sessionURL, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
        
        // Create subdirectories
        try fileManager.createDirectory(at: sessionURL.appendingPathComponent("audio"))
        try fileManager.createDirectory(at: sessionURL.appendingPathComponent("input_data"))
        try fileManager.createDirectory(at: sessionURL.appendingPathComponent("thumbnails"))
        
        return sessionURL
    }
}
```

## Performance Optimization

### Memory Management

#### Buffer Pool Implementation
```swift
actor FrameBufferPool {
    private var availableBuffers: [CVPixelBuffer] = []
    private let maxBufferCount: Int
    private let bufferAttributes: [String: Any]
    
    func acquireBuffer() -> CVPixelBuffer? {
        if let buffer = availableBuffers.popLast() {
            return buffer
        }
        
        // Create new buffer if pool not at capacity
        guard availableBuffers.count < maxBufferCount else { return nil }
        
        var pixelBuffer: CVPixelBuffer?
        let status = CVPixelBufferCreate(
            kCFAllocatorDefault,
            1920, 1080,
            kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA,
            bufferAttributes as CFDictionary,
            &pixelBuffer
        )
        
        return status == kCVReturnSuccess ? pixelBuffer : nil
    }
    
    func returnBuffer(_ buffer: CVPixelBuffer) {
        guard availableBuffers.count < maxBufferCount else { return }
        availableBuffers.append(buffer)
    }
}
```

#### Resource Monitoring
```swift
class PerformanceMonitor: ObservableObject {
    @Published var cpuUsage: Double = 0
    @Published var memoryUsage: UInt64 = 0
    @Published var diskUsage: UInt64 = 0
    @Published var frameDropCount: Int = 0
    
    private let updateTimer = Timer.publish(every: 1.0, on: .main, in: .common).autoconnect()
    
    init() {
        updateTimer
            .sink { _ in
                Task { await self.updateMetrics() }
            }
            .store(in: &cancellables)
    }
    
    private func updateMetrics() async {
        // Monitor system resource usage
        cpuUsage = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
        memoryUsage = getMemoryUsage()
        diskUsage = getDiskUsage()
    }
}
```

### Concurrent Processing

#### Task Coordination
```swift
actor RecordingCoordinator {
    private var videoTask: Task<Void, Error>?
    private var audioTask: Task<Void, Error>?
    private var inputTask: Task<Void, Error>?
    
    func startRecording() async throws {
        // Launch concurrent recording tasks
        videoTask = Task { try await processVideoStream() }
        audioTask = Task { try await processAudioStream() }
        inputTask = Task { try await processInputEvents() }
        
        // Monitor for completion or errors
        _ = try await withThrowingTaskGroup(of: Void.self) { group in
            group.addTask { try await self.videoTask!.value }
            group.addTask { try await self.audioTask!.value }
            group.addTask { try await self.inputTask!.value }
            
            try await group.waitForAll()
        }
    }
}
```

## Error Handling and Logging

### Comprehensive Error System
```swift
enum RecordingError: LocalizedError, CustomStringConvertible {
    case permissionDenied(PermissionType)
    case insufficientDiskSpace(required: UInt64, available: UInt64)
    case audioDeviceUnavailable(deviceID: String)
    case encodingFailed(underlying: Error)
    case systemResourcesUnavailable
    
    var errorDescription: String? {
        switch self {
        case .permissionDenied(let type):
            return "Permission required for \(type.rawValue)"
        case .insufficientDiskSpace(let required, let available):
            return "Need \(required)MB, only \(available)MB available"
        // ... other cases
        }
    }
}
```

### Structured Logging
```swift
import OSLog

extension Logger {
    static let recording = Logger(subsystem: "it.didyouget.mac", category: "Recording")
    static let audio = Logger(subsystem: "it.didyouget.mac", category: "Audio")
    static let input = Logger(subsystem: "it.didyouget.mac", category: "Input")
    static let performance = Logger(subsystem: "it.didyouget.mac", category: "Performance")
}

// Usage throughout the application
Logger.recording.info("Recording session started with configuration: \(configuration)")
Logger.performance.warning("Frame drop detected: \(frameDropCount) frames")
```

Ready to learn about configuration options? Continue to [Configuration & Settings](configuration.md) for complete customization guidance.

# 8. Troubleshooting

## Common Issues and Solutions

### Installation and Setup Issues

#### Application Won't Launch
**Problem:** "Did You Get It" cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified.

**Solution:**
```bash
# Remove quarantine attribute
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Did You Get It.app"

# Or allow in System Preferences
# System Preferences → Security & Privacy → General → Allow "Did You Get It"
# Click "Open Anyway" if prompted
```

**Problem:** App crashes immediately on launch with error in Console.

**Diagnostic Steps:**
```bash
# Check system logs
log show --predicate 'process == "Did You Get It"' --last 10m

# Check crash reports
ls ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Did\ You\ Get\ It*

# Verify app integrity
codesign -v "/Applications/Did You Get It.app"
```

**Common Causes and Fixes:**
- **Corrupted download**: Re-download from official source
- **Insufficient macOS version**: Requires macOS 13.0+
- **Missing dependencies**: Reinstall app or system updates
- **Conflicting software**: Disable other screen recording apps

#### Permission Issues
**Problem:** Recording fails with permission errors.

**Complete Permission Setup:**
```bash
# Check current permissions
tccutil list | grep "Did You Get It"

# Reset permissions (requires restart)
tccutil reset ScreenCapture it.didyouget.mac
tccutil reset Microphone it.didyouget.mac
tccutil reset Accessibility it.didyouget.mac

# Manual permission grant via System Preferences:
# 1. System Preferences → Security & Privacy → Privacy
# 2. Screen Recording → Check "Did You Get It"
# 3. Microphone → Check "Did You Get It" (if using audio)
# 4. Accessibility → Check "Did You Get It" (for input tracking)
```

**Permission Troubleshooting Script:**
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# permission_check.sh

echo "Checking Did You Get It permissions..."

# Check screen recording permission
if tccutil list | grep -q "kTCCServiceScreenCapture.*Did You Get It.*ALLOWED"; then
    echo "✅ Screen Recording: GRANTED"
else
    echo "❌ Screen Recording: DENIED - Please enable in System Preferences"
fi

# Check microphone permission
if tccutil list | grep -q "kTCCServiceMicrophone.*Did You Get It.*ALLOWED"; then
    echo "✅ Microphone: GRANTED"
else
    echo "⚠️  Microphone: DENIED - Enable if you need audio recording"
fi

# Check accessibility permission
if tccutil list | grep -q "kTCCServiceAccessibility.*Did You Get It.*ALLOWED"; then
    echo "✅ Accessibility: GRANTED"
else
    echo "❌ Accessibility: DENIED - Required for input tracking"
fi
```

### Recording Quality Issues

#### Poor Video Quality or Stuttering
**Problem:** Video appears pixelated, stuttering, or dropping frames.

**Diagnostic Information:**
```swift
// Check recording metrics in debug mode
struct RecordingDiagnostics {
    let actualFrameRate: Double
    let targetFrameRate: Int
    let droppedFrames: Int
    let memoryUsage: UInt64
    let cpuUsage: Double
    let diskWriteSpeed: Double
}
```

**Performance Optimization Steps:**

1. **Lower Recording Settings:**
```bash
# Reduce frame rate
dygi config set --frame-rate=30

# Lower resolution
dygi config set --resolution=1080p

# Disable unnecessary features
dygi config set --mouse-precision=low --audio=false
```

2. **System Optimization:**
```bash
# Close unnecessary applications
killall "Chrome" "Slack" "Discord"

# Check available disk space (need >5GB free)
df -h

# Monitor system resources
top -o cpu -l 3 | grep "Did You Get It"
```

3. **Hardware Recommendations:**
- **Minimum**: 8GB RAM, Intel i5 or Apple M1
- **Recommended**: 16GB RAM, Apple M1 Pro/Max or Intel i7
- **Storage**: SSD with >10GB free space

#### Audio Sync Issues
**Problem:** Audio and video are out of sync in recordings.

**Audio Sync Troubleshooting:**
```swift
// Debug audio-video synchronization
class AudioVideoSyncDiagnostic {
    func checkSyncOffset() {
        let videoTimestamp = videoProcessor.lastFrameTimestamp
        let audioTimestamp = audioProcessor.lastSampleTimestamp
        let offset = abs(videoTimestamp - audioTimestamp)
        
        if offset > 0.1 { // >100ms offset
            Logger.audio.warning("Sync offset detected: \(offset)s")
        }
    }
}
```

**Solutions:**
1. **Use system audio only** (most reliable sync)
2. **Check audio device sample rates** (ensure 48kHz)
3. **Close other audio applications**
4. **Restart Core Audio:**
```bash
sudo launchctl kickstart -kp system/com.apple.audio.coreaudiod
```

### Input Tracking Problems

#### Mouse/Keyboard Events Not Recorded
**Problem:** Input tracking data files are empty or incomplete.

**Input Tracking Diagnostic:**
```swift
class InputTrackingDiagnostic {
    func diagnoseInputTracking() {
        // Check if accessibility permission is granted
        let trusted = AXIsProcessTrusted()
        print("Accessibility trusted: \(trusted)")
        
        // Test event monitoring
        let monitor = NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEventsMatching([.mouseMoved]) { event in
            print("Mouse event detected: \(event.locationInWindow)")
        }
        
        if monitor == nil {
            print("❌ Failed to create event monitor")
        }
    }
}
```

**Troubleshooting Steps:**
1. **Check Accessibility Permission:** System Preferences → Security & Privacy → Accessibility
2. **Restart the application** after granting permissions
3. **Test with simple movements:** Move mouse slowly and check if events are captured
4. **Check for interfering software:** Disable other input monitoring tools

#### Inaccurate Mouse Coordinates
**Problem:** Mouse coordinates don't match actual screen positions.

**Coordinate System Issues:**
```swift
// Debug coordinate transformations
func debugCoordinateSystem() {
    let screenFrame = NSScreen.main?.frame ?? .zero
    let mouseLocation = NSEvent.mouseLocation
    
    print("Screen frame: \(screenFrame)")
    print("Mouse location: \(mouseLocation)")
    print("Flipped Y: \(screenFrame.height - mouseLocation.y)")
}
```

**Common Causes:**
- **Multiple displays** with different scaling factors
- **Retina scaling** not accounted for
- **Coordinate system flipping** (macOS uses bottom-left origin)

**Fix:**
```swift
// Correct coordinate transformation
func correctMouseCoordinates(_ location: NSPoint) -> NSPoint {
    guard let screen = NSScreen.main else { return location }
    
    // Account for Retina scaling
    let scaleFactor = screen.backingScaleFactor
    let correctedX = location.x * scaleFactor
    
    // Flip Y coordinate (macOS uses bottom-left origin)
    let correctedY = (screen.frame.height - location.y) * scaleFactor
    
    return NSPoint(x: correctedX, y: correctedY)
}
```

### Performance and Resource Issues

#### High CPU Usage
**Problem:** "Did You Get It" consumes excessive CPU resources.

**CPU Usage Analysis:**
```bash
# Monitor CPU usage by thread
top -pid $(pgrep "Did You Get It") -l 5

# Detailed process analysis
sample "Did You Get It" 10 -f ~/Desktop/cpu_sample.txt

# Check for runaway threads
spindump "Did You Get It" -o ~/Desktop/spindump.txt
```

**CPU Optimization:**
```swift
// Implement frame rate throttling
class PerformanceManager {
    private let cpuThreshold: Double = 0.7
    
    func adjustSettingsForPerformance() {
        let currentCPU = getCurrentCPUUsage()
        
        if currentCPU > cpuThreshold {
            // Reduce frame rate
            recordingSettings.frameRate = max(24, recordingSettings.frameRate - 10)
            
            // Lower input tracking frequency
            inputSettings.samplingRate = max(30, inputSettings.samplingRate / 2)
            
            Logger.performance.info("Reduced settings due to high CPU usage: \(currentCPU)")
        }
    }
}
```

#### Memory Leaks
**Problem:** Memory usage continuously increases during recording.

**Memory Diagnostic Tools:**
```bash
# Monitor memory usage
memory_pressure

# Detailed memory analysis with Xcode Instruments
# Or use built-in diagnostic
leaks "Did You Get It"

# Check for excessive buffer allocation
vmmap $(pgrep "Did You Get It") | grep "MALLOC"
```

**Memory Leak Prevention:**
```swift
// Proper buffer management
class FrameBufferManager {
    private var bufferPool: [CVPixelBuffer] = []
    private let maxBuffers = 10
    
    func acquireBuffer() -> CVPixelBuffer? {
        defer { cleanupOldBuffers() }
        
        if let buffer = bufferPool.popLast() {
            return buffer
        }
        
        return createNewBuffer()
    }
    
    func returnBuffer(_ buffer: CVPixelBuffer) {
        guard bufferPool.count < maxBuffers else { return }
        bufferPool.append(buffer)
    }
    
    private func cleanupOldBuffers() {
        // Prevent excessive buffer accumulation
        while bufferPool.count > maxBuffers {
            bufferPool.removeFirst()
        }
    }
}
```

### File and Export Issues

#### Recording Files Corrupted or Unplayable
**Problem:** Output video files won't play or appear corrupted.

**File Integrity Check:**
```bash
# Check video file integrity
ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height,duration recording.mov

# Verify file wasn't truncated
ls -la recording.mov
file recording.mov

# Test playback with different players
quicktime-player recording.mov
vlc recording.mov
ffplay recording.mov
```

**Recovery Options:**
```bash
# Attempt file repair with FFmpeg
ffmpeg -i corrupted_recording.mov -c copy -avoid_negative_ts make_zero repaired_recording.mov

# Extract usable frames from partial file
ffmpeg -i partial_recording.mov -r 1 frame_%04d.png

# Recover audio track separately
ffmpeg -i recording.mov -vn -acodec copy audio_track.wav
```

#### Large File Sizes
**Problem:** Recording files are unexpectedly large.

**File Size Analysis:**
```bash
# Analyze video properties
ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_streams recording.mov | jq '.streams[]'

# Calculate expected file size
# Formula: (width × height × fps × duration × bit_depth) / 8 / compression_ratio
```

**Size Optimization:**
```bash
# Post-recording compression
ffmpeg -i large_recording.mov \
    -c:v libx264 \
    -crf 23 \
    -preset medium \
    -c:a aac \
    -b:a 128k \
    optimized_recording.mp4

# Reduce resolution while maintaining quality
ffmpeg -i recording.mov \
    -vf scale=1920:1080 \
    -c:v libx264 \
    -crf 20 \
    scaled_recording.mp4
```

## Advanced Diagnostics

### System Compatibility Check

#### Compatibility Diagnostic Script
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# system_compatibility.sh

echo "=== Did You Get It System Compatibility Check ==="

# Check macOS version
MACOS_VERSION=$(sw_vers -productVersion)
echo "macOS Version: $MACOS_VERSION"

if [[ $(echo "$MACOS_VERSION >= 13.0" | bc -l) -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo "✅ macOS version compatible"
else
    echo "❌ macOS 13.0+ required"
fi

# Check hardware
HARDWARE=$(system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep "Model Name" | cut -d: -f2 | xargs)
echo "Hardware: $HARDWARE"

# Check available RAM
RAM_GB=$(system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep "Memory:" | awk '{print $2}')
echo "RAM: ${RAM_GB}GB"

if [[ ${RAM_GB%.*} -ge 8 ]]; then
    echo "✅ Sufficient RAM"
else
    echo "⚠️  8GB+ RAM recommended"
fi

# Check disk space
DISK_SPACE=$(df -h / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
echo "Available Disk Space: $DISK_SPACE"

# Check ScreenCaptureKit availability
if [[ $(echo "$MACOS_VERSION >= 12.3" | bc -l) -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo "✅ ScreenCaptureKit available"
else
    echo "❌ ScreenCaptureKit requires macOS 12.3+"
fi
```

### Network and Firewall Issues

#### Network Diagnostic (for CLI/API features)
```bash
# Check if CLI service is running
lsof -i :8080 | grep "Did You Get It"

# Test local API connectivity
curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/status

# Check firewall rules
/usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --getglobalstate
```

### Debug Logging

#### Enable Verbose Logging
```swift
// Enable debug logging in preferences
struct DebugSettings {
    static var verboseLogging = false
    static var logLevel: LogLevel = .info
    
    enum LogLevel: String, CaseIterable {
        case debug = "DEBUG"
        case info = "INFO" 
        case warning = "WARNING"
        case error = "ERROR"
    }
}

// Usage in application
Logger.recording.debug("Frame processed: \(frameNumber), timestamp: \(timestamp)")
```

#### Access Debug Logs
```bash
# Application logs location
tail -f ~/Library/Logs/DidYouGetIt/application.log

# System logs
log show --predicate 'subsystem == "it.didyouget.mac"' --last 1h

# Export logs for support
log collect --start '2024-01-15 14:00:00' --output ~/Desktop/didyougetit_logs.logarchive
```

## Getting Help and Support

### Information to Gather Before Reporting Issues

#### System Information Script
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# gather_system_info.sh

echo "=== Did You Get It Support Information ==="
echo "Generated: $(date)"
echo

echo "System Information:"
sw_vers
echo

echo "Hardware:"
system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep -E "(Model Name|Processor|Memory|Graphics)"
echo

echo "Permissions:"
tccutil list | grep "Did You Get It"
echo

echo "Recent Crashes:"
ls -la ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Did\ You\ Get\ It* 2>/dev/null | tail -5
echo

echo "Disk Space:"
df -h /
echo

echo "Running Processes:"
ps aux | grep -i "did you get it\|screen.*record\|capture"
```

#### Bug Report Template
When reporting issues, please include:

1. **System Information:**
   - macOS version
   - Hardware model
   - Available RAM and disk space

2. **Application Information:**
   - Did You Get It version
   - Installation method (direct download, build from source)
   - Configuration settings used

3. **Problem Description:**
   - What you were trying to do
   - What happened instead
   - Steps to reproduce
   - Frequency of occurrence

4. **Logs and Diagnostics:**
   ```bash
   # Gather comprehensive diagnostic info
   ./gather_system_info.sh > support_info.txt
   
   # Include recent logs
   tail -100 ~/Library/Logs/DidYouGetIt/application.log >> support_info.txt
   ```

# Quick performance optimization
echo "Running performance optimization..."

# 1. Close unnecessary applications

# 2. Free up RAM

# 3. Check and optimize recording settings

echo "Performance optimization complete!"

# 4. User Interface

## Design Philosophy

### Minimal Interface Principles

#### Less is More
Did You Get It embodies extreme minimalism in its user interface design:

```swift
// Core UI principle: Essential controls only
struct ContentView: View {
    @StateObject private var recordingManager = RecordingManager.shared
    
    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 20) {
            if recordingManager.isRecording {
                RecordingIndicator()
            } else {
                RecordingControls()
            }
        }
        .frame(width: 300, height: 200)
        .background(.ultraThinMaterial)
    }
}
```

**Key Design Decisions:**
- **Single-window interface**: No complex multi-panel layouts
- **Context-sensitive controls**: Show only relevant options
- **Immediate actions**: One-click recording start/stop
- **Visual feedback**: Clear status indication without clutter

#### Keyboard-First Workflow
The interface is designed to minimize mouse interaction:

```swift
// Keyboard shortcuts are primary interaction method
.keyboardShortcut("r", modifiers: .command) // Start/Stop recording
.keyboardShortcut(",", modifiers: .command) // Preferences
.keyboardShortcut("q", modifiers: .command) // Quit
```

### Main Interface Components

#### Recording Control Panel

**Primary Controls**
```swift
struct RecordingControls: View {
    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 16) {
            // Large, prominent record button
            RecordButton()
                .frame(width: 80, height: 80)
            
            // Essential status information
            StatusDisplay()
            
            // Quick access settings
            QuickSettings()
        }
    }
}
```

**Record Button States**
- **Ready**: Large red circle, pulsing subtly
- **Recording**: Red square with stop icon, solid color
- **Processing**: Spinner with progress indication
- **Error**: Orange triangle with alert icon

#### Status Display Area

**Real-Time Information**
```swift
struct StatusDisplay: View {
    @ObservedObject var recorder: RecordingManager
    
    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 20) {
            // Recording duration
            Text(recorder.formattedDuration)
                .font(.system(.title2, design: .monospaced))
            
            // Performance indicators
            PerformanceIndicators()
            
            // Storage space warning
            if recorder.lowDiskSpace {
                DiskSpaceWarning()
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**Status Elements:**
- **Recording timer**: MM:SS format, updates every second
- **Frame rate indicator**: Current FPS with target comparison
- **Audio levels**: System and microphone input meters
- **Storage space**: Available disk space warning
- **Performance warning**: CPU/memory usage alerts

#### Quick Settings Panel

**Immediate Access Controls**
```swift
struct QuickSettings: View {
    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 12) {
            // Recording area selector
            AreaSelector()
            
            // Audio source toggles
            AudioToggle(source: .system)
            AudioToggle(source: .microphone)
            
            // Input tracking toggle
            InputTrackingToggle()
        }
        .buttonStyle(.borderless)
    }
}
```

### Recording Area Visualization

#### Area Selection Overlay

**Visual Feedback System**
```swift
class AreaSelectionOverlay: NSView {
    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
        // Semi-transparent overlay with recording area highlight
        NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.3).setFill()
        bounds.fill()
        
        // Clear recording area
        NSColor.clear.setFill()
        recordingRect.fill(using: .clear)
        
        // Animated border around recording area
        drawAnimatedBorder()
    }
}
```

**Interactive Elements:**
- **Selection handles**: Drag to resize recording area
- **Dimension display**: Real-time width/height values
- **Grid alignment**: Snap to pixel boundaries
- **Window detection**: Highlight application windows

#### Multi-Display Handling

**Display Selection Interface**
```swift
struct DisplaySelector: View {
    @State private var selectedDisplay: DisplayInfo?
    
    var body: some View {
        VStack {
            ForEach(DisplayManager.shared.availableDisplays) { display in
                DisplayPreview(display: display)
                    .overlay(
                        display.isSelected ? SelectionIndicator() : nil
                    )
                    .onTapGesture {
                        selectedDisplay = display
                    }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Preferences Interface

#### Settings Organization

**Tabbed Settings Panel**
```swift
struct PreferencesView: View {
    var body: some View {
        TabView {
            RecordingSettings()
                .tabItem { Label("Recording", systemImage: "record.circle") }
            
            AudioSettings()
                .tabItem { Label("Audio", systemImage: "speaker.wave.2") }
            
            InputSettings()
                .tabItem { Label("Input", systemImage: "keyboard") }
            
            OutputSettings()
                .tabItem { Label("Output", systemImage: "folder") }
            
            AdvancedSettings()
                .tabItem { Label("Advanced", systemImage: "gearshape") }
        }
        .frame(width: 600, height: 400)
    }
}
```

#### Recording Settings Tab

**Video Configuration**
```swift
struct RecordingSettings: View {
    @AppStorage("frameRate") private var frameRate: Int = 60
    @AppStorage("resolution") private var resolution: String = "native"
    
    var body: some View {
        Form {
            Section("Video Quality") {
                Picker("Frame Rate", selection: $frameRate) {
                    Text("24 FPS").tag(24)
                    Text("30 FPS").tag(30)
                    Text("60 FPS").tag(60)
                }
                
                Picker("Resolution", selection: $resolution) {
                    Text("Native Retina").tag("native")
                    Text("Scaled Retina").tag("scaled")
                    Text("1080p HD").tag("1080p")
                    Text("Custom").tag("custom")
                }
            }
            
            Section("Recording Area") {
                RecordingAreaControls()
            }
        }
    }
}
```

#### Audio Settings Tab

**Audio Source Configuration**
```swift
struct AudioSettings: View {
    @AppStorage("systemAudioEnabled") private var systemAudio = true
    @AppStorage("microphoneEnabled") private var microphone = false
    
    var body: some View {
        Form {
            Section("Audio Sources") {
                Toggle("System Audio", isOn: $systemAudio)
                Toggle("Microphone", isOn: $microphone)
                
                if microphone {
                    MicrophoneSelector()
                    InputLevelMeter()
                }
            }
            
            Section("Audio Quality") {
                AudioQualitySettings()
            }
            
            Section("Audio Processing") {
                Toggle("Noise Reduction", isOn: $noiseReduction)
                Toggle("Auto Gain Control", isOn: $autoGain)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Menu Bar Integration

#### Menu Bar Icon States

**Status Indication**
```swift
class MenuBarController: NSObject {
    private let statusItem = NSStatusBar.system.statusItem(withLength: NSStatusItem.variableLength)
    
    func updateIcon(for state: RecordingState) {
        switch state {
        case .idle:
            statusItem.button?.image = NSImage(systemSymbolName: "record.circle")
        case .recording:
            statusItem.button?.image = NSImage(systemSymbolName: "stop.circle.fill")
            statusItem.button?.image?.isTemplate = false
        case .processing:
            statusItem.button?.image = NSImage(systemSymbolName: "gear")
        }
    }
}
```

**Menu Bar Menu**
```swift
struct MenuBarMenu: View {
    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
            // Quick actions
            Button("Start Recording") { startRecording() }
                .keyboardShortcut("r", modifiers: .command)
            
            Button("Open Preferences") { openPreferences() }
                .keyboardShortcut(",", modifiers: .command)
            
            Divider()
            
            // Recent recordings
            Menu("Recent Recordings") {
                ForEach(recentRecordings) { recording in
                    Button(recording.name) {
                        NSWorkspace.shared.open(recording.url)
                    }
                }
            }
            
            Divider()
            
            Button("Quit") { NSApplication.shared.terminate(nil) }
                .keyboardShortcut("q", modifiers: .command)
        }
    }
}
```

### Recording Session UI

#### Recording Indicator

**Minimal Recording Feedback**
```swift
struct RecordingIndicator: View {
    @State private var pulseAnimation = false
    
    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 12) {
            // Pulsing red dot
            Circle()
                .fill(.red)
                .frame(width: 12, height: 12)
                .scaleEffect(pulseAnimation ? 1.2 : 1.0)
                .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 1).repeatForever(), value: pulseAnimation)
            
            // Recording duration
            Text(recordingDuration)
                .font(.system(.title2, design: .monospaced))
                .foregroundColor(.primary)
        }
        .onAppear { pulseAnimation = true }
    }
}
```

#### Performance Overlay (Optional)

**Developer Mode Display**
```swift
struct PerformanceOverlay: View {
    @ObservedObject var metrics: RecordingMetrics
    
    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
            Text("FPS: \(metrics.currentFPS, specifier: "%.1f")")
            Text("Memory: \(metrics.memoryUsage)MB")
            Text("CPU: \(metrics.cpuUsage, specifier: "%.1f")%")
        }
        .font(.system(.caption, design: .monospaced))
        .padding(8)
        .background(.ultraThinMaterial)
        .cornerRadius(8)
    }
}
```

### Accessibility Features

#### VoiceOver Support

**Screen Reader Integration**
```swift
// Proper accessibility labels and hints
Button("Start Recording") { }
    .accessibilityLabel("Start screen recording")
    .accessibilityHint("Begins capturing screen content and input events")

Toggle("System Audio", isOn: $systemAudio)
    .accessibilityLabel("Record system audio")
    .accessibilityValue(systemAudio ? "Enabled" : "Disabled")
```

#### Keyboard Navigation

**Full Keyboard Control**
```swift
// Tab navigation through all controls
.focusable()
.onKeyPress(.tab) { _ in
    focusNextControl()
    return .handled
}

// Escape key cancellation
.onKeyPress(.escape) { _ in
    cancelCurrentOperation()
    return .handled
}
```

### Error and Status Communication

#### User-Friendly Error Messages

**Error Display System**
```swift
struct ErrorAlert: View {
    let error: RecordingError
    
    var body: some View {
        Alert(
            "Recording Error",
            message: Text(error.userFriendlyDescription),
            primaryButton: .default(Text("Retry")) {
                retryRecording()
            },
            secondaryButton: .cancel()
        )
    }
}
```

**Error Categories:**
- **Permission errors**: Clear guidance to system settings
- **Performance warnings**: Suggestions for quality adjustments
- **Storage issues**: Disk space and location problems
- **Hardware errors**: Audio/video device unavailability

#### Status Notifications

**Non-Intrusive Feedback**
```swift
// Subtle notifications for state changes
Text("Recording saved successfully")
    .foregroundColor(.secondary)
    .transition(.opacity.combined(with: .slide))
    .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: showNotification)
```

### Customization Options

#### Interface Themes

**Theme Selection**
```swift
enum InterfaceTheme: CaseIterable {
    case system, light, dark, minimal
    
    var colorScheme: ColorScheme? {
        switch self {
        case .system: return nil
        case .light: return .light
        case .dark: return .dark
        case .minimal: return .dark
        }
    }
}
```

#### Layout Preferences

**Interface Density Options**
- **Compact**: Minimal spacing, small controls
- **Standard**: Default comfortable layout
- **Spacious**: Larger targets, more spacing

<source>test-and-release.sh</source>
<document_content>
#!/bin/bash

# test-and-release.sh - Complete test and release workflow
# Usage: ./test-and-release.sh [version]

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

# Check if version is provided
if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <version>"
    echo "Example: $0 1.1.0"
    exit 1
fi

VERSION="$1"
VERSION_TAG="v$VERSION"

# Validate version format
if ! [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    echo "❌ Invalid version format. Use semantic versioning (e.g., 1.1.0)"
    exit 1
fi

echo "🚀 Starting test and release workflow for version $VERSION"

# Check if we're on the main branch
CURRENT_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$CURRENT_BRANCH" != "main" ]; then
    echo "⚠️  Warning: You're not on the main branch. Current branch: $CURRENT_BRANCH"
    read -p "Do you want to continue? (y/N) " -n 1 -r
    echo
    if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
        echo "❌ Aborted"
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# Check if working directory is clean
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
    echo "❌ Working directory is not clean. Please commit or stash changes."
    git status --short
    exit 1
fi

# Run full test suite
echo "🧪 Running full test suite..."
./build.sh debug --test --clean

# Check if tag already exists
if git tag -l | grep -q "^$VERSION_TAG$"; then
    echo "❌ Tag $VERSION_TAG already exists"
    exit 1
fi

# Build release version
echo "📦 Building release version..."
./build.sh release --test

# Create and push tag
echo "🏷️  Creating tag $VERSION_TAG..."
git tag -a "$VERSION_TAG" -m "Release version $VERSION"

echo "📤 Pushing tag to origin..."
git push origin "$VERSION_TAG"

echo "✅ Release workflow complete!"
echo "   Version: $VERSION"
echo "   Tag: $VERSION_TAG"
echo "   Release package: release/DidYouGet-$VERSION-macos.tar.gz"

# Check for GitHub CLI and create release
if command -v gh &> /dev/null; then
    echo "🐙 GitHub CLI detected. Creating GitHub release..."
    
    # Create release notes
    RELEASE_NOTES="Release $VERSION

## Changes
$(git log --pretty=format:"- %s" $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 HEAD^)..HEAD)

## Installation
Download the \`DidYouGet-$VERSION-macos.tar.gz\` file, extract it, and run the executable.

## Requirements
- macOS 13.0 or later"
    
    gh release create "$VERSION_TAG" \
        --title "Release $VERSION" \
        --notes "$RELEASE_NOTES" \
        "release/DidYouGet-$VERSION-macos.tar.gz"
    
    echo "✅ GitHub release created!"
else
    echo "ℹ️  GitHub CLI not found. Please create the release manually on GitHub."
fi

echo "🎉 All done!"
</document_content>
</document>
